definition_en: a young person, especially a boy or girl between childhood and adult life
core_image: 巷子里骑着车飞过的那个半大孩子，衣服还短一截
scene: 傍晚巷口一群半大孩子在追球，喊声一直传到楼上。 A few youngsters were playing football in the school yard after class.
sceneCN: 这里 youngster 是「年轻人；孩子」（第 1 个义项：介于童年与成年之间的年轻人）；句意为放学后几个孩子在操场踢球。巷子里骑车飞过的半大孩子，就是这个词的印象。

collocations.zh: 一个前途看好的年轻人

derivatives.zh: youngster 的基础词，义为「年轻的」
同根名词，义为「青春；青年人」

senses.title: The young person
senses.definition: a young person, used especially of children and teenagers in an informal tone
senses.definitionCN: 年轻的人，尤指儿童与十几岁的少年，语气随意
senses.example: A few youngsters were playing football in the school yard after class.
senses.exampleCN: 放学后几个孩子在操场踢球。
senses.why: The suffix -ster once marked a person, so young plus -ster simply means the one who is young.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ster 过去用来标人，所以 young 加 -ster 就是「年轻的那个人」。

senses.title: The young lad
senses.definition: a boy or young man, often said with warmth or a touch of familiarity
senses.definitionCN: 男孩子或年轻男子，常带亲切或熟稔的语气
senses.example: The youngster at the counter helped me find the right ticket.
senses.exampleCN: 柜台后的小伙子帮我找到了对的车票。
senses.why: Because the word names a person rather than a stage, it fits friendly address as easily as description.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词称的是人而不是阶段，所以既能客观描述也能亲切称呼。

senses.title: The young animal
senses.definition: a young animal, used in farming and in writing about wildlife
senses.definitionCN: 年幼的动物，用于农事与描写野生动物的文字
senses.example: The keeper fed the youngsters before the park opened.
senses.exampleCN: 饲养员在公园开门前先喂了那些幼崽。
senses.why: The word for a young person is extended to animals whenever the writer wants a warm tone.
senses.whyCN: 只要作者想要温暖的语气，用来指年轻人的词就会延伸到动物身上。

senses.title: The member of the team
senses.definition: a young member of a team or group, often contrasted with the experienced ones
senses.definitionCN: 队伍或团体中年轻的一员，常与老队员对照
senses.example: Two youngsters in the squad scored in the second half.
senses.exampleCN: 队里两名年轻球员在下半场进了球。
senses.why: In a group of mixed ages, the word picks out the younger ones, so it becomes a role as well as a stage.
senses.whyCN: 在年龄混合的群体里，这个词挑出较年轻的那些，于是它既是阶段也是角色。

senses.title: The person of little experience
senses.definition: a person new to a job or trade, used with a hint of judgement
senses.definitionCN: 刚进入某行业或工作的人，带一点评判意味
senses.example: He was still a youngster in the trade and asked many questions.
senses.exampleCN: 他在这行还算新手，问了很多问题。
senses.why: Youth stands for inexperience as well as for age, so the word can weigh someone in a profession too.
senses.whyCN: 年轻不仅指年龄也指经验少，所以这个词也能用来衡量一个人在行业里的分量。

intro.en: Youngster is young plus the old suffix -ster, which once named the person who did or was something.
intro.cn: youngster 是 young 加上古老后缀 -ster，这个后缀过去用来指做某事或具有某特征的人。

items.en: The suffix -estre named a woman of a trade or role, as in bæcestre, a baker.
items.cn: 后缀 -estre 用来指从事某行业或角色的女性，如 bæcestre 即女面包师。

items.en: The suffix reduced to -ster and spread to male agents and to people of a kind.
items.cn: 后缀简化为 -ster，扩用到男性施动者以及某类人身上。

items.en: Youngster appeared in the sixteenth century as a plain word for a young person.
items.cn: youngster 于十六世纪出现，是「年轻人」的普通说法。

items.en: The word spread to animals and to team members in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 二十世纪这个词扩用到动物与队伍成员上。

items.en: Today it is mostly informal, and youth remains the neutral noun.
items.cn: 今天它多为口语，中性的名词仍是 youth。

note.en: Youngster sits among several words that name young people with different tones.
note.cn: youngster 处在几个语气不同、都指年轻人的词之间。

entries.definition: not old, of few years
the young period or young people
a person who plays tricks
entries.definitionCN: 同一后缀构成的词，骗子

entries.definition: a person between thirteen and nineteen
entries.definitionCN: 近义，十三到十九岁的人

entries.definition: a child, in informal speech
a fully grown person

normalIntro.en: The suffix -ster turns a quality into a person, and youngster is a clean example.
normalIntro.cn: 后缀 -ster 把性质变成人，youngster 就是一个干净的例子。

normal.en: Compare trickster: trick plus -ster gives a person who tricks, so young plus -ster gives one who is young.
normal.cn: 对照 trickster：trick 加 -ster 是会耍花招的人，所以 young 加 -ster 就是年轻的人。

normal.en: The suffix began in Old English as -estre and named women in trades, then widened to all people.
normal.cn: 这个后缀在古英语作 -estre，指从业的女性，后来扩到所有人。

normal.en: The plural is simply youngsters, so the word behaves like any regular noun.
normal.cn: 复数就是 youngsters，和普通名词一样。

normal.en: Youth is the neutral noun, while youngster is warmer and more spoken.
normal.cn: youth 是中性的名词，youngster 更温暖也更口语。

normal.en: In sport writing, youngsters often means the young players on a team rather than children.
normal.cn: 在体育报道里，youngsters 常指队里的年轻球员，而不是小孩。

abstract.en: Picture a boy on a bicycle rounding the corner too fast, coat sleeves too short.
abstract.cn: 想象一个男孩骑车太快地拐过街角，袖子短了一截。

abstract.en: Picture a group of small figures chasing a ball until the light goes.
abstract.cn: 想象一群小身影追着球，一直追到天黑。

abstract.en: Picture a new worker asking the third question of the morning, notebook open.
abstract.cn: 想象一个新员工早上已经在问第三个问题，本子摊着。

examples.en: A few youngsters were playing football in the school yard after class.
examples.cn: 放学后几个孩子在操场踢球。

examples.en: The youngster at the counter helped me find the right ticket.
examples.cn: 柜台后的小伙子帮我找到了对的车票。

examples.en: Two youngsters in the squad scored in the second half.
examples.cn: 队里两名年轻球员在下半场进了球。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「羊子的」——山坡上一群小羊蹦来蹦去，那就是羊崽子，跟说「那帮年轻的」一个口气，于是 youngster 指年轻人。

root: young（年轻，古英语 geong）加后缀 -ster（古英语 -estre，指从事某事或具有某特征的人）。

sensesIntro.en: One quality turned into a person easily spreads from children to a friendly lad, to animals, to team members, and to the inexperienced.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个变成人的性质，很容易从孩子扩到亲切的小伙子、动物、队里的队员，以及经验少的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a half-grown child rushing past
core.cn: 核心意象：一个半大孩子匆匆跑过

branches.en: A young person is the plain, original sense.
branches.cn: 年轻人是这个词朴素的本义。

branches.en: Personhood rather than age lets the word serve as warm address.
branches.cn: 称的是人而不是年龄，所以它能用作亲切的称呼。

branches.en: The warm tone carries over to young animals.
branches.cn: 温暖的语气延伸到了动物的幼崽。

branches.en: In a mixed group, the word picks out the younger members.
branches.cn: 在年龄混合的群体里，这个词挑出较年轻的成员。

branches.en: Youth also means inexperience, which gives the word a judging edge.
branches.cn: 年轻也意味着经验少，于是这个词带上评判色彩。

intro.en: Youngster is built with -ster, a suffix that has made agent nouns for more than a thousand years.
intro.cn: youngster 由 -ster 构成，这个后缀造施动名词已有一千多年。

latinIntro.en: Latin made similar age words with -anus and with iuvenis; English kept its own -ster instead.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 -anus 和 iuvenis 造类似的年龄词，英语则保留了自己的 -ster。

items.meaning: one who is or does something
items.meaningCN: 表示某类人或从事某事的人
items.example: A trickster plays tricks on others.
The youngsters waited by the gate.
The story is about a clever trickster.
items.exampleCN: 这故事讲一个聪明的骗子。

items.meaning: a member of a criminal gang

items.example: Old English bæcestre meant a female baker.
items.exampleCN: 古英语 bæcestre 指女面包师。
拉丁语 iuvenis 给出 juvenile。

items.example: Youth is no excuse for rudeness.

definition_zh: 任何…都；丝毫（用于否定或强调）；whatever 的强调形式
definition_en: a stronger form of whatever, used after a negative or a question to mean not any at all
core_image: 一根空手指一直指到尽头，什么都没碰到
scene: 他把口袋翻出来抖了抖，连一枚硬币都没有掉下来。 He had no doubt whatsoever that the train would be late.
sceneCN: 这里 whatsoever 是「丝毫」（第 1 个义项：加强否定，表示一点也不）；句意为他丝毫也不怀疑火车会晚点。把口袋翻空、一根手指指到尽头全无着落，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 丝毫；根本（用于否定加强）
无论什么（whatever 的强调形式）

senses.title: Not any at all
senses.definition: used at the end of a negative statement to mean not even the smallest amount
senses.definitionCN: 用在否定陈述之后，表示连最小的一点也没有
senses.example: He had no doubt whatsoever that the train would be late.
senses.exampleCN: 他丝毫也不怀疑火车会晚点。
senses.why: So adds emphasis to ever, so the suffix doubles its strength, and after no it reaches zero.
senses.whyCN: so 给 ever 添了强调，词尾因此力量加倍，放在 no 之后便直达零点。

senses.title: The heavy version of whatever
senses.definition: used in formal writing where whatever would carry less weight
senses.definitionCN: 用于正式书面语，表示比 whatever 更强调
senses.example: Whatsoever you choose, the committee will review it.
senses.exampleCN: 无论你选什么，委员会都会审阅。
senses.why: The longer form survives mostly in legal and religious prose, where a heavier sound suggests a wider scope.
senses.whyCN: 这个较长的形式主要存活在法律与宗教文本中，更重的音暗示更宽的范围。

senses.title: Of any kind
senses.titleCN: 任何种类的（用于疑问或条件句）
senses.definition: used after a noun in questions or conditional clauses to mean of any sort
senses.definitionCN: 用在疑问句或条件从句的名词之后，表示任何种类
senses.example: Is there any evidence whatsoever for that claim?
senses.exampleCN: 那个说法有任何证据吗？
senses.why: A negative form and a doubtful question are two faces of the same emptiness, so the word fits both.
senses.whyCN: 否定形式与疑问语气是同一片空无的两面，所以这个词两者都合。

intro.en: Whatsoever is a three-part compound of what, so and ever, and it was fixed in English by the time of the early Bible translations.
intro.cn: whatsoever 由 what、so、ever 三段复合而成，在早期圣经译本的时代已经在英语中定型。

items.en: The three elements stood apart: hwæt, swā and æfre, each with its own meaning.
items.cn: 三个成分彼此分开：hwæt、swā、æfre，各有自己的意思。

items.en: Writers joined whatever first, then slipped so into the middle to make the strongest form.
items.cn: 作者先合成 whatever，再把 so 插进中间，造出最强的形式。

items.en: The King James Bible of 1611 spread whatsoever through English worship and legal language.
items.cn: 1611 年的钦定版圣经让 whatsoever 随礼拜与法律语言传遍英语世界。

items.en: Spoken English mostly dropped it, but legal writing kept it for its weight at the end of a negative clause.
items.cn: 现代口语大多舍弃了它，但法律文本为它在否定从句末尾留住分量。

items.en: Today it survives in phrasings such as no doubt whatsoever and none whatsoever.
items.cn: 今天它存活于 no doubt whatsoever、none whatsoever 等说法中。

note.en: The first group gathers words that look close to whatsoever, the second the words for anything at all and for nothing.
note.cn: 第一组收外形接近 whatsoever 的词，第二组收表示「任何」与「全无」的说法。

entries.definition: The shorter everyday form of the same word.
entries.definitionCN: 同词的较短的日常形式

entries.definition: The same pattern applied to who, also archaic in tone.
entries.definitionCN: who 的同一模式，语气同样古旧

entries.definition: Any one from a set, without the so.
Slightly, with a completely different meaning.
The most common phrase for the same strengthening.
Not one, often followed by whatsoever.
Completely, carrying the emphatic force into positive sentences.

normalIntro.en: Count the three parts: what, so, ever. The middle so is the weight that makes the word heavy.
normalIntro.cn: 数这三段：what、so、ever。中间的 so 是把词压重的那块石头。

normal.en: Take whatever and drop so into its middle, and you get the heavier word.
normal.cn: 把 whatever 拆开，往中间塞进 so，就得到更重的这个词。

normal.en: It likes the end of a negative: no doubt whatsoever, none whatsoever.
normal.cn: 它爱待在否定句末尾：no doubt whatsoever、none whatsoever。

normal.en: The King James Bible kept this heavy sound in English for four centuries.
normal.cn: 钦定版圣经把这沉重的声音在英语里保存了四百年。

normal.en: Somewhat looks like it, but means a little instead of not at all.
normal.cn: somewhat 看着像它，却表示「有点」而不是「全无」。

normal.en: Lawyers still use it because it closes every door at once.
normal.cn: 律师仍用它，因为它一下关住所有的门。

abstract.en: Feel a pocket turned out and shaken empty.
abstract.cn: 感觉口袋被翻过来抖到空。

abstract.en: See a finger reach and touch nothing at the end.
abstract.cn: 看一根手指伸到头，什么都没碰到。

abstract.en: Hear a gavel make the last word heavy.
abstract.cn: 听法槌最后一下把语气压重。

examples.en: She had no idea whatsoever where the letter had gone.
examples.cn: 她一点也不知道那封信去哪儿了。

examples.en: Nothing whatsoever was left in the room.
examples.cn: 房间里什么也没留下。

examples.en: Any changes whatsoever must be reported first.
examples.cn: 任何改动都必须先报告。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「沃特搜艾佛」——沃特搜了一辈子，什么都没搜到，丝毫也没有。

root: 中古英语 what + so + ever 三段复合；同族有 whatever、whosoever。

sensesIntro.en: The word is whatever with a weight added, so it starts as the strongest not any at all, survives in formal writing as a heavier whatever, and fits doubt as well as denial.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词是加了分量的 whatever，先是最强的「丝毫也不」，又在书面语中作为更重的 whatever 存活，既配否定也配疑问。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fingertip reaching the end of a shelf and finding nothing.
core.cn: 核心意象：指尖摸到架子尽头，什么也没有。

branches.en: The denial branch: no doubt whatsoever.
branches.cn: 否定分支：毫无疑义。

branches.en: The formal branch: whatsoever you choose.
branches.cn: 书面分支：无论你选什么。

branches.en: The question branch: any evidence whatsoever.
branches.cn: 疑问分支：任何证据。

branches.en: The legal branch: none whatsoever in a contract.
branches.cn: 法律分支：合同里的 none whatsoever。

branches.en: The religious branch: whatsoever kept in old Bible prose.
branches.cn: 宗教分支：旧圣经文字中保留的 whatsoever。

intro.en: Whatsoever is a three-part compound, and its weight comes from the middle so between what and ever.
intro.cn: whatsoever 是三段复合词，其重量来自夹在 what 与 ever 之间的 so。

latinIntro.en: Latin formed the same emphasis with quicumque and its parts; the entries below give the borrowed parallel, not the source of whatsoever.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 quicumque 及其组成成分表达同样的强调；下面的条目给出借入的并行说法，而非 whatsoever 的来源。

items.example: It is the heavy stone in the middle.
items.exampleCN: 它是中间那块压重的石头。

items.example: It is the lighter everyday form.
It does the same job in plain speech.
items.exampleCN: 它在日常口语中做同样的工作。

items.example: It often takes whatsoever after it.

items.exampleCN: 它带着同样的强调成分 -so-。

definition_zh: 天然的；粗糙的；粗鲁的；粗略的
definition_en: in a raw natural state, made without skill, or said without tact
core_image: 从井口直接舀起的一勺原油，还混着泥沙
scene: 工地上有人从桶里舀出一勺还混着泥沙的原油。 They loaded the crude oil straight onto the truck.
sceneCN: 这里 crude 指「天然的、未加工的」（第 1 个义项：从地下取出后还没提炼的）；句意是他们把原油直接装上卡车。

pos.zh: 天然的；粗糙的；粗鲁的；粗略的

senses.title: Raw, unrefined
senses.definition: in a natural state and not yet processed
senses.definitionCN: 处于自然状态、尚未加工的
senses.example: The refinery turns crude oil into fuel.
senses.exampleCN: 炼油厂把原油变成燃料。
senses.why: What comes out of the ground must be cleaned before use.
senses.whyCN: 从地下出来的东西，用前总要先洗净。

senses.title: Roughly made
senses.definition: made quickly and without skill or care
senses.definitionCN: 做得快而缺乏技艺或用心
senses.example: He built a crude shelter from branches.
senses.exampleCN: 他用树枝搭了个粗糙的棚子。
senses.why: Untrained hands leave their marks on what they make.
senses.whyCN: 没练过的手，会在做的东西上留下痕迹。

senses.title: Rude, without tact
senses.definition: said or done in a way that shocks or offends people
senses.definitionCN: 以令人震惊或冒犯的方式说出或做出
senses.example: His crude remark silenced the room.
senses.exampleCN: 他那句粗鲁的话让全场安静下来。
senses.why: A missing polish in words cuts like a rough edge.
senses.whyCN: 话里少了打磨，就像毛边一样割人。

intro.en: Crude comes from Latin crudus, raw or unripe, through Old French crud.
intro.cn: crude 源自拉丁语 crudus（生的、未熟的），经古法语 crud 进入英语。

items.en: Crudus described food that was raw or not cooked.
items.cn: crudus 形容生的、没煮过的食物。

items.en: It also meant unripe, or hard to digest.
items.cn: 它也表示未成熟、难以消化。

items.en: Crud kept both the raw and the unripe senses.
items.cn: crud 同时保留了生与未熟两层意思。

items.en: Crude first described raw food and unripe fruit.
items.cn: crude 最初形容生食与未熟的水果。

items.en: It spread to rough work and rude words.
items.cn: 它扩展到粗糙的手艺与粗鲁的言语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cru- opening, and the meaning group names things still in a raw state.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cru- 开头，近义组列出仍处于原始状态的说法。

entries.definition: the hard outer layer of bread
a very small piece of bread
willing to cause pain
not cooked or processed
not smooth or carefully finished
entries.definitionCN: 不平滑或未精细完成的

entries.definition: showing no respect

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with something pulled from the ground and end with words that cut.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一件刚出土的东西开始，落到几句会割人的话上。

normal.en: Crude is the state before the factory touches it.
normal.cn: crude 是工厂还没碰过它时的状态。

normal.en: A crude chair still holds you up, but it wobbles.
normal.cn: 粗糙的椅子仍能撑住你，只是会晃。

normal.en: Crude words are words with the polish sanded off.
normal.cn: 粗鲁的话，是被磨掉了光的那层话。

normal.en: Raw oil, raw wood, raw manners: one word for all.
normal.cn: 原油、原木、没教养的举止：一个词全包。

normal.en: If it came straight out and skipped the finishing, it is crude.
normal.cn: 直接从里面出来、跳过了修饰的，就是 crude。

abstract.en: Picture oil black and thick, still smoking from the well.
abstract.cn: 想象又黑又稠的油，从井口还冒着气。

abstract.en: Picture a table made of one unplaned board.
abstract.cn: 想象一张只用一块没刨过的板做成的桌子。

abstract.en: Picture a laugh that lands on the wrong face.
abstract.cn: 想象一声笑落在不该落的那张脸上。

examples.en: The crude oil is refined before it is sold.
examples.cn: 原油在出售前要先提炼。

examples.en: He made a crude table from three old boards.
examples.cn: 他用三块旧木板做了一张粗糙的桌子。

examples.en: Her crude comment hurt everyone at the table.
examples.cn: 她那句粗鲁的评论伤了在座所有人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 crude 记成「生的」：原油、生手、生硬的话，都还没经过打磨。

root: 源自拉丁语 crudus（生的、未熟的），经古法语 crud 进入英语；本义是未经烹煮与提炼，后来引申为做得粗糙、说话粗鲁。

sensesIntro.en: From raw material, to rough work, to words that wound.
sensesIntro.cn: 从没加工的原料，到粗糙的手艺，再到伤人的话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bucket of oil lifted straight from the well.
core.cn: 核心意象：一桶刚从井里提上来的原油。

branches.en: What the earth gives is used before it is cleaned.
branches.cn: 大地给出的东西，还没洗净就被用上。

branches.en: A thing made in a hurry keeps its rough edges.
branches.cn: 匆忙做出来的东西，会留着粗糙的边。

branches.en: A remark without polish can cut the listener.
branches.cn: 没打磨过的话，会割到听的人。

branches.en: Raw material and rough work share one word.
branches.cn: 原料与粗活共用一个词。

branches.en: Rough edges appear in things and in manners.
branches.cn: 粗糙的边既出现在物件上，也出现在举止里。

intro.en: Crude belongs to the Latin crudus family, where raw matter and rough manners meet.
intro.cn: crude 属于拉丁语 crudus 这一族，原料与粗鲁在这里相遇。

latinIntro.en: The Latin crudus, raw or unripe, is the root under all these words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 crudus（生的、未熟的）是这些词共同的根。

items.example: Crude oil burns with dark smoke.
The crudity of the plan shocked us.

items.example: The crudeness of the joke upset her.

items.example: Wash that crud off your hands.

items.meaning: raw vegetables served as a dish

definition_en: the way information is arranged, the design of a page or book, or to prepare a disk for use
core_image: 屏幕上整齐排列的文字、图片与留白
scene: 请把报告排成标准格式。 Please set the report in the standard format.
sceneCN: 这里 format 是「格式」（第 1 个义项）；句意：请把报告排成标准格式。

senses.title: Arrangement of data
senses.definition: the way data or information is arranged
senses.definitionCN: 数据或信息的排列方式
senses.example: Please set the report in the standard format.
senses.exampleCN: 请把报告排成标准格式。
senses.why: This is the central technical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心的技术义项。

senses.title: Page design
senses.definition: the size, shape, and design of a page or book
senses.definitionCN: 页面或书籍的尺寸、形状与设计
senses.example: The magazine changed its format.
senses.exampleCN: 这本杂志改了版式。
senses.why: Printing gave format its visual sense.
senses.whyCN: 印刷术赋予 format 视觉义项。

senses.title: A plan of events
senses.definition: the way an event or program is organized
senses.definitionCN: 活动或节目的组织方式
senses.example: The show has a new format.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节目有了新的安排。
senses.why: The idea of arrangement extends to events.
senses.whyCN: 排列的概念延伸到活动。

senses.title: To prepare a disk
senses.definition: to prepare a disk or device for storing data
senses.definitionCN: 为存储数据而准备磁盘或设备
senses.example: He formatted the drive.
senses.exampleCN: 他把硬盘格式化了。
senses.why: Computing turned the noun into a verb.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域把名词转化为动词。

intro.en: Format comes from a Latin word for a shaped thing.
intro.cn: format 来自拉丁语中表示成形之物的词。

items.en: Formatus meant shaped or formed.
items.cn: formatus 意为成形的或被塑造的。

items.en: Format named the shape of a printed book.
items.cn: format 指印刷书籍的版式。

items.en: It came to mean the arrangement of any content.
items.cn: 它逐渐表示任何内容的安排。

items.en: Broadcasting borrowed it for program plans.
items.cn: 广播行业借用它表示节目安排。

items.en: Computing added the sense of preparing a disk.
items.cn: 计算机领域增添了准备磁盘的义项。

note.en: Format is compared with similar-looking words and with words for arrangement.
note.cn: 把 format 与形近词以及表示安排的词作比较。

entries.definition: official or ceremonial
the process of forming
earlier or previous
the way things are arranged on a page
the order in which things are placed
a particular way of doing something

normalIntro.en: Format is the frame that holds content in place.
normalIntro.cn: format 是把内容固定在合适位置的框架。

normal.en: Please set the report in the standard format.
normal.cn: 请把报告排成标准格式。

normal.en: The magazine changed its format.
normal.cn: 这本杂志改了版式。

normal.en: The show has a new format.
normal.cn: 这个节目有了新的安排。

normal.en: He formatted the drive.
normal.cn: 他把硬盘格式化了。

normal.en: Choose the right file format.
normal.cn: 选择合适的文件格式。

abstract.en: Format is a promise about where things will be.
abstract.cn: 格式是关于事物将在何处的承诺。

abstract.en: A clear format lets content speak.
abstract.cn: 清晰的格式让内容自己说话。

abstract.en: Even empty space is part of the design.
abstract.cn: 连空白也是设计的一部分。

examples.en: Please set the report in the standard format.

examples.en: The magazine changed its format.
examples.cn: 这本杂志改了版式。

examples.en: He formatted the drive.
examples.cn: 他把硬盘格式化了。

dict_mnemonic.text: format 和 form 同源：先有一个形状，再按这个形状排列内容，就成了格式。

root: 源自拉丁语 formatus（成形的），核心义「内容所遵循的排列形态」。

sensesIntro.en: Format means the arrangement of data, page design, a program plan, or to prepare a disk.
sensesIntro.cn: format 意为格式、版式、安排或格式化。

core.en: Content placed inside a fixed frame.
core.cn: 被放进固定框架中的内容。

branches.en: Data follows a pattern.
branches.cn: 数据遵循一种模式。

branches.en: The page has a shape.
branches.cn: 页面有自己的形状。

branches.en: The program follows a plan.
branches.cn: 节目遵循一个安排。

branches.en: The disk is made ready.
branches.cn: 磁盘被准备好。

branches.en: Screen and page share the same frame.
branches.cn: 屏幕与纸页共享同一个框架。

intro.en: Format builds a small family of arrangement words.
intro.cn: format 构成表示排列的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Format comes from Latin formatus; the Latin entry below shows that source.
latinIntro.cn: format 来自拉丁语 formatus；下面的拉丁条目展示了这一来源。

items.example: The format is easy to read.

items.meaningCN: 格式（复数）；格式化（第三人称单数）

格式化程序修正了间距。

items.meaning: the type of a computer file
items.example: The file format is not supported.

latinEntries.example: Formatus is the Latin source of format.
latinEntries.exampleCN: formatus 是 format 的拉丁语来源。

definition_en: used before a number to show that it is not exact, or to describe something as nearly but not exactly so
core_image: 秤杆停在差一点水平的位置
scene: 她在站台上看了好几次表。 The journey takes approximately two hours.
sceneCN: 这里 approximately 是「大约」（第 1 个义项：用于数量或时间的不精确估计）；句意是这段路程大约要两个小时。

senses.title: About, before a number
senses.definition: used to give a figure that is close to the true one
senses.definitionCN: 给出一个接近真实值的数字
senses.example: The repair will take approximately three days.
senses.exampleCN: 这次修理大约要三天。
senses.why: The suffix -ly turns the adjective approximate into a marker placed before figures that are nearest rather than exact.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ly 把形容词 approximate 变成标记词，专门放在那些「最接近而非精确」的数字前面。

senses.title: In a broadly similar way
senses.definition: used when two things are nearly, but not exactly, the same
senses.definitionCN: 用于说明两件事大体相同但并不完全一致
senses.example: The two methods are approximately equivalent in cost.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种方法在成本上大致相当。
senses.why: From counting, the word extends to comparing qualities: two things may stand near each other without matching exactly.
senses.whyCN: 从计数扩展到性质比较：两样东西可以彼此靠得很近，却并不完全吻合。

intro.en: Approximately is simply the adjective approximate with the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: approximately 就是形容词 approximate 加上副词后缀 -ly。

items.en: prope meant 'near'.
items.cn: prope 意为「近」。

items.en: The superlative proximus meant 'nearest'.
items.cn: 最高级 proximus 意为「最近的」。

items.en: approximare meant 'to come near'.
items.cn: approximare 意为「靠近」。

items.en: English formed the adjective approximate from the Latin verb.
items.cn: 英语由这个拉丁动词造出形容词 approximate。

items.en: Adding -ly produced the everyday adverb for rough figures.
items.cn: 加上 -ly 之后，形成了日常用来修饰约数的副词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the root; the near-meaning group gives other hedges for numbers.
note.cn: 形近组同根；近义组是其他用来给数字留余地的词。

entries.definition: nearly exact
a rough value
near rather than exact
roughly
without precision
almost

normalIntro.en: Approximately softens a number so it is not a promise.
normalIntro.cn: approximately 让数字变得柔和，不再像承诺。

normal.en: It usually sits right before the figure.
normal.cn: 它通常紧挨在数字前面。

normal.en: In speech people often shorten it to about.
normal.cn: 口语里人们常把它换成 about。

normal.en: The adjective form drops the -ly.
normal.cn: 形容词形式去掉 -ly。

normal.en: It can also compare two things as broadly equal.
normal.cn: 它也能表示两件事大体相等。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: ap-PROX-i-mate-ly.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：ap-PROX-i-mate-ly。

abstract.en: See a needle stopping a hair below the mark.
abstract.cn: 想象指针停在刻度下方一点点。

abstract.en: See two lines that almost, not quite, meet.
abstract.cn: 想象两条几乎相接却未相接的线。

abstract.en: See a hand waving to mean roughly so.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手左右摆动表示大概如此。

examples.en: The journey takes approximately two hours.
examples.cn: 这段路程大约要两个小时。

examples.en: The repair will take approximately three days.
examples.cn: 这次修理大约要三天。

examples.en: The two methods are approximately equivalent in cost.
examples.cn: 这两种方法在成本上大致相当。

dict_mnemonic.text: approximate（近似的）加 -ly：以近似的方式，就是大约。

root: 由形容词 approximate 加副词后缀 -ly 构成；approximate 源自拉丁语 approximare「靠近」，其词根 proximus 意为「最近的」。

sensesIntro.en: One adverb covers both a rough figure and a rough match between things.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个副词既修饰粗略的数字，也描述事物之间大致的吻合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a weighing scale resting a little off level.
core.cn: 核心意象：一架天平略微偏离水平。

branches.en: approximately ten minutes
branches.cn: 大约十分钟

branches.en: approximately half
branches.cn: 大约一半

branches.en: approximately equal
branches.cn: 大致相等

branches.en: approximately the same size
branches.cn: 大小大致相同

branches.en: approximately correct
branches.cn: 大致正确

intro.en: An adverb made by adding -ly to a Latin-derived adjective.
intro.cn: 这是一个由拉丁来源形容词加 -ly 构成的副词。

latinIntro.en: The root prope, 'near', also lies behind proximity.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 prope「近」也是 proximity 的来源。

definition_en: to make someone feel sad, to lower a level or value, or to press something down
core_image: 一只手掌按在弹簧上，弹簧一点点被压短
scene: 消息传来，屋里没人说话，有人把脸埋进手里。 The bad news depressed everyone in the room.
sceneCN: 这里 depress 指「使沮丧」（第 1 个义项：让人情绪低落）；句意是坏消息让屋里所有人都很沮丧。

senses.title: Make someone sad
senses.definition: to make a person feel low and unhappy
senses.definitionCN: 让人情绪低落、不快乐
senses.example: The bad news depressed everyone in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 坏消息让屋里所有人都很沮丧。
senses.why: A feeling can be pressed down like a spring.
senses.whyCN: 心情也能像弹簧一样被压下去。

senses.title: Lower a level or value
senses.definition: to reduce the amount, price or strength of something
senses.definitionCN: 减少某物的数量、价格或强度
senses.example: A flood of imports depressed prices.
senses.exampleCN: 大量进口压低了价格。
senses.why: A market also has a level, and it can be pushed under.
senses.whyCN: 市场也有水位，也能被按到下面。

senses.title: Press down
senses.definition: to push something down with your hand or foot
senses.definitionCN: 用手或脚把某物向下压
senses.example: Depress the pedal slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 慢慢踩下踏板。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: a plain downward push.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的意思：一个朴素的向下推。

intro.en: Depress comes from Latin deprimere, built from de-, down, and premere, to press.
intro.cn: depress 来自拉丁语 deprimere，由 de-（向下）与 premere（压）组成。

items.en: Deprimere joined de-, meaning down, with premere, to press.
items.cn: deprimere 由 de-（向下）与 premere（压）合成。

items.en: It described pushing something physically downward.
items.cn: 它描述把某物在物理上向下压。

items.en: English used depress for pressing down.
items.cn: 英语用 depress 表示向下压。

items.en: Trade gave it the sense of lowering prices and spirits.
items.cn: 商业给了它压低价格与情绪的意思。

items.en: Now it covers mood, money and buttons.
items.cn: 如今它覆盖心情、金钱与按钮。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the depress stem, and the meaning group gives three downward actions.
note.cn: 形近组共用 depress 词干，近义组则给出三种向下的动作。

entries.definition: feeling very low and unhappy
making people feel low
a long low mood or a low economy
entries.definitionCN: 长期低落的情绪或低迷的经济

entries.definition: to make someone feel sad
to move something down
to push firmly against something

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a thumb on a spring and end with a market that has lost its level.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从按在弹簧上的拇指开始，落到一个失去水平线的市场。

normal.en: De- is down and press is press: to press down.
normal.cn: de- 是向下，press 是压，合起来就是往下压。

normal.en: Bad news works like a hand on a spring.
normal.cn: 坏消息的作用，就像一只手按在弹簧上。

normal.en: A price can be depressed without anyone touching it.
normal.cn: 价格可以在没人碰它的情况下被压低。

normal.en: A button and a mood both go down under pressure.
normal.cn: 按钮和心情，都会在压力下下去。

normal.en: Depress is the verb behind depressed and depression.
normal.cn: depress 是 depressed 与 depression 背后的动词。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pushing a metal spring shorter and shorter.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把金属弹簧越压越短。

abstract.en: Picture a room where everyone looks at the floor.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋里，所有人都看着地面。

abstract.en: Picture a foot easing a pedal down.
abstract.cn: 想象一只脚慢慢把踏板踩下。

examples.en: The bad news depressed everyone in the room.
examples.cn: 坏消息让屋里所有人都很沮丧。

examples.en: A flood of imports depressed prices.
examples.cn: 大量进口压低了价格。

examples.en: Depress the pedal slowly.
examples.cn: 慢慢踩下踏板。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 depress 记成「往下压」：de 是向下，press 是压，把人的心情往下压，就是使沮丧。

root: 来自拉丁语 deprimere，由 de-（向下）与 premere（压）组成。它先表示把东西向下压，十四世纪进入英语；十七世纪商业又给了它压低价格的意思，同时也用来形容情绪被压下去。

sensesIntro.en: From a hand pressing a spring, to prices falling, to a pedal going down.
sensesIntro.cn: 从手压弹簧，到价格下落，再到踏板被踩下。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a palm flattens a spring until it cannot rise.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手掌把弹簧按到再也弹不起来。

branches.en: The first sense is a feeling pushed down out of sight.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是被按到看不见的心情。

branches.en: The second sense is a number pushed to a lower level.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是被按到更低位置的数字。

branches.en: The third sense is the plain physical push.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是最朴素的物理推压。

branches.en: The language treats a mood as something with a surface.
branches.cn: 这种语言把心情当成有表面的东西。

branches.en: A price and a pedal both go down when force is applied.
branches.cn: 价格与踏板，受力时都会往下走。

intro.en: Depress stands at the centre of a family of low moods, low prices and chemical depressants.
intro.cn: depress 站在一族词的中心，周围是低落的情绪、低迷的价格与抑制类药物。

latinIntro.en: The base is premere, to press, with de- meaning down.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是 premere（压），前缀 de- 表示向下。

items.meaning: to push down or make low
items.example: Do not depress the red switch.

items.meaning: a low mood or a low economy
in a way that lowers the mood
a substance that slows the body
a drug that lifts low mood
items.exampleCN: 医生给他换了抗抑郁药。

definition_en: a conclusion reached from evidence, or the act of reaching it
core_image: 桌上一张空椅子、一杯冷茶，人走了
scene: 房间里灯还亮着，人却不见了。 Her silence was an inference that the answer was no.
sceneCN: 这里 inference 是「推断出的结论」（第 1 个义项：由证据得出的判断）；句意是她的沉默让人推断答案是「不」。

pos.zh: 名词：推断；推论；结论；推理过程

senses.title: A conclusion from evidence
senses.definition: a judgement you form because of clues rather than on direct information
senses.definitionCN: 因线索而形成的判断，而非依据直接信息
senses.example: The police drew a simple inference from the wet shoes.
senses.exampleCN: 警方从那双湿鞋作出一个简单的推断。
senses.why: The noun names what the verb produces, a conclusion carried in from evidence.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名动词所产出的东西：从证据里带进来的结论。

senses.title: The act of reasoning
senses.definition: the mental act of moving from evidence to a conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 从证据走向结论的心理活动
senses.example: Inference is slower than seeing and often more careful.
senses.exampleCN: 推论比看见慢，也常常更谨慎。
senses.why: -ence can name either the result or the activity, and here it names both.
senses.whyCN: -ence 既能指结果也能指活动，这里两者兼有。

senses.title: A method in science
senses.definition: a formal procedure for reaching conclusions in logic or statistics
senses.definitionCN: 在逻辑或统计中得出正式结论的方法
senses.example: Statistical inference allows us to judge a whole population from a sample.
senses.exampleCN: 统计推断让我们从样本判断总体。
senses.why: When rules are fixed, the activity becomes a named method.
senses.whyCN: 当规则固定下来，这种活动就成为一个有名目的方法。

senses.title: Something read between the lines
senses.definition: a meaning understood but not stated
senses.definitionCN: 被理解却未被明说的含义
senses.example: The inference from her letter was clear: she would not come.
senses.exampleCN: 她信中隐含的意思很清楚：她不会来。
senses.why: Unspoken meaning has to be built by the reader, so it too is an inference.
senses.whyCN: 未说出的含义要由读者建构，因此它也是 infer 的结果。

senses.title: A guess, if weak
senses.definition: an uncertain conclusion reached with too little evidence
senses.definitionCN: 证据不足时得出的不确定结论
senses.example: That was an inference, not a fact.
senses.exampleCN: 那只是推断，并不是事实。
senses.why: The noun reminds us that a conclusion without proof still carries risk.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词提醒我们：没有证据的结论仍有风险。

intro.en: Inference is the English noun of infer, from Latin inferre, to bring in, as in a conclusion into an argument.
intro.cn: inference 是 infer 的英语名词形式，出自拉丁语 inferre（带入），如同把结论带入论证。

items.en: Inferre meant to bring in, on in- plus ferre, to carry.
items.cn: inferre 意为带入，由 in- 加 ferre（携带）构成。

items.en: In grammar and logic, inferre could name the idea that follows from words.
items.cn: 在语法与逻辑中，inferre 可指由词句推出的想法。

items.en: The noun reached French before English took it in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 这个名词先进入法语，十六世纪再由英语吸收。

items.en: Inference became the standard word in logic for a step from premises.
items.cn: inference 成为逻辑中表示「从前提出发的一步」的标准词。

items.en: The plural inferences covers everyday guesses as well as formal proofs.
items.cn: 复数 inferences 既指日常猜测，也指正式证明。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the infer family; the near-meaning group holds words for conclusions.
note.cn: 形近组收 infer 词族；近义组收表示结论的词。

entries.definition: To reach a conclusion from evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「推断」，是本词的原形。

entries.definition: Based on reasoning.
The act of getting in the way.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「干扰」，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A conclusion drawn by logic.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「演绎；推论」，偏逻辑推导。

entries.definition: A judgement reached after thought.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「结论」，是最通用的说法。

entries.definition: An answer given without certainty.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「猜测」，证据更少。

normalIntro.en: The hooks tie the noun to its verb, its adjective and the set phrases used in exams and science.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把名词与动词、形容词以及考试和科学中的固定说法连起来。

normal.en: Infer is the verb and inference is the noun: draw an inference.
normal.cn: infer 是动词，inference 是名词：draw an inference。

normal.en: The -ence ending marks a state or act, as in difference and patience.
normal.cn: -ence 词尾标示状态或行为，如 difference、patience。

normal.en: By inference means not by direct statement but by reasoning.
normal.cn: by inference 意为不是听来的，而是推出来的。

normal.en: Statistical inference is the formal version, judging a population from a sample.
normal.cn: statistical inference 是正式用法：从样本判断总体。

normal.en: Inferential swaps -ence for -ial and becomes the adjective of logic.
normal.cn: inferential 把 -ence 换成 -ial，成为逻辑意义上的形容词。

abstract.en: An inference is a bridge no one built for you; you build it from the clues.
abstract.cn: 推断是一座没人替你搭的桥，你从线索里自己搭。

abstract.en: The word means carried in: what the mind carries from the world to itself.
abstract.cn: 这个词意为「带进来」：心灵从世界带向自身的东西。

abstract.en: Every inference is a small promise that the world is consistent.
abstract.cn: 每一个推断都是一个小承诺：世界是前后一致的。

examples.en: The report draws a clear inference about the cause of the fire.
examples.cn: 报告对火灾原因作出了明确的推断。

examples.en: We should not base an inference on so little evidence.
examples.cn: 我们不该凭这么少的证据下推断。

examples.en: Her inference was correct: the letter never arrived.
examples.cn: 她的推断是对的：那封信从未寄到。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因佛认死」——因为拜了佛就认定死理，全凭推断。

root: infer（推断）+ -ence（名词后缀）；词根为拉丁 ferre（携带）。

sensesIntro.en: Inference can mean the conclusion, the act of concluding, the formal method, the meaning read between lines, or a weak guess.
sensesIntro.cn: inference 既可指结论本身，也可指得出结论的动作、正式的方法、读出的言外之意，或证据不足的猜测。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cold cup of tea and an empty chair.
core.cn: 核心意象：一杯冷茶和一张空椅子。

branches.en: RESULT LINE: the conclusion itself.
branches.cn: 结果线：结论本身。

branches.en: ACT LINE: the mental step from clue to answer.
branches.cn: 动作线：从线索到答案的心理一步。

branches.en: METHOD LINE: fixed rules in logic and statistics.
branches.cn: 方法线：逻辑与统计中的固定规则。

branches.en: IMPLICIT LINE: meaning read from what was not said.
branches.cn: 隐含线：从没说出口的话里读出含义。

branches.en: RISK LINE: a conclusion may still be wrong.
branches.cn: 风险线：结论仍可能是错的。

intro.en: A noun ending in -ence built on the Latin verb of carrying.
intro.cn: 一个以 -ence 结尾、建立在拉丁「携带」动词上的名词。

latinIntro.en: The root ferre, to carry, also gives conference, reference and interference.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 ferre（携带）也产生了 conference、reference 与 interference。

definition_en: the main stalk of a plant, or to stop something from spreading
core_image: 一朵花挺立在细长的花茎上
scene: 花茎被风吹断了。 The flower stem broke in the wind.
sceneCN: 这里 stem 是「茎」（第 1 个义项）；句意：花茎被风吹断了。

senses.title: Plant stalk
senses.definition: the main thin part of a plant that supports leaves or flowers
senses.definitionCN: 植物支撑叶或花的主要细长部分
senses.example: The flower stem broke in the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 花茎被风吹断了。
senses.why: This is the physical plant sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是植物的实体义项。

senses.title: Word base
senses.definition: the part of a word to which endings are added
senses.definitionCN: 词中加词尾的那部分
senses.example: The stem of the word is shown in bold.
senses.exampleCN: 这个词的词干用粗体标出。
senses.why: A plant stem supports growth, and a word stem supports new forms.
senses.whyCN: 植物茎支撑生长，词干支撑新形式。

senses.title: Stop the spread
senses.definition: to stop something from growing or spreading
senses.definitionCN: 阻止某物生长或扩散
senses.example: They tried to stem the flow of water.
senses.exampleCN: 他们设法堵住水流。
senses.why: To hold back the current is to stem it.
senses.whyCN: 挡住水流，就是 stem 它。

senses.title: Come from
senses.definition: to have something as its origin
senses.definitionCN: 以某物为来源
senses.example: The problem stems from poor planning.
senses.exampleCN: 问题源于规划不当。
senses.why: A branch grows from a stem, so a result stems from a cause.
senses.whyCN: 枝从茎上长出，结果也从原因上长出。

intro.en: Stem comes from Old English stemn, the trunk or stalk of a plant.
intro.cn: stem 来自古英语 stemn，指植物的主干或茎。

items.en: The root named a tree trunk.
items.cn: 该词根指树干。

items.en: Stemn meant the stalk of a plant.
items.cn: stemn 指植物的茎。

items.en: Stem also named the base of a word.
items.cn: stem 也指词的基部。

items.en: To stem became to check a flow.
items.cn: to stem 变成「挡住水流」。

items.en: Stem from named the source of a result.
items.cn: stem from 指结果的来源。

note.en: Stem is compared with look-alike words and with words for plant parts and origins.
note.cn: 把 stem 与形近词以及表示植物部位和来源的词作比较。

entries.definition: a movement of the foot
water vapour
serious and strict
a plant stem
the part below ground
to stop or slow something

normalIntro.en: Stem holds up a flower, then holds up a word, then holds back a flood.
normalIntro.cn: stem 先托起一朵花，再托起一个词，最后挡住一场洪水。

normal.en: Cut the stem just above a leaf.
normal.cn: 在叶子稍上方剪断茎。

normal.en: The word has a Latin stem.
normal.cn: 这个词有拉丁词干。

normal.en: They worked to stem the flood.
normal.cn: 他们努力堵住洪水。

normal.en: The trouble stems from one mistake.
normal.cn: 麻烦源于一个错误。

normal.en: Stem cells can grow into many kinds of cells.
normal.cn: 干细胞能长成多种细胞。

abstract.en: Every branch remembers the stem it left.
abstract.cn: 每一根枝条，都记得它离开的茎。

abstract.en: To stem a flow is to stand still against motion.
abstract.cn: 挡住水流，就是站着不动去对抗流动。

abstract.en: Where a result comes from is where its cure begins.
abstract.cn: 结果来自哪里，解药也从哪里开始。

examples.en: The flower stem broke in the wind.
examples.cn: 花茎被风吹断了。

examples.en: The problem stems from poor planning.
examples.cn: 问题源于规划不当。

examples.en: They tried to stem the flow of water.
examples.cn: 他们设法堵住水流。

dict_mnemonic.text: stem 本义是植物的「茎」，也指单词的「词干」；作动词是「阻止、遏制」，stem from 表示「源于」，两者是四级高频用法。

root: 来自古英语 stemn（茎、树干），源于日耳曼语；由植物的支撑部位引申为词干，再由「挡住流向」引申为遏止，由「枝从茎出」引申为源于。

sensesIntro.en: Stem is a plant stalk, a word base, a check on a flow, or the source a result comes from.
sensesIntro.cn: stem 是植物茎、词干、对流动的遏止，或结果所来自的源头。

core.en: A stalk that holds a plant up.
core.cn: 把植物撑起来的茎。

branches.en: A flower sits at the top of a thin stalk.
branches.cn: 一朵花立在细茎顶端。

branches.en: Endings attach to a bare base.
branches.cn: 词尾接在一个裸词干上。

branches.en: Sandbags hold a river steady.
branches.cn: 沙袋把河水挡住。

branches.en: A problem shows where its root lies.
branches.cn: 问题显出它的根源在哪里。

branches.en: The stalk is both a support and a beginning.
branches.cn: 茎既是支撑，也是开端。

intro.en: Stem takes plural and verb endings, and builds a negative adjective.
intro.cn: stem 加复数与动词词尾，并构成否定形容词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.meaning: had a stem or was checked

items.exampleCN: 干细胞也许能修复组织。

items.example: The fear stems from the past.
They tried to stem the tide.
items.exampleCN: 他们设法遏制这股潮流。

definition_en: to rub a hard edge against a surface, to wound the skin, to barely succeed, or to gather with effort
core_image: 勺子贴着锅底刮过，留下一圈亮亮的痕迹
scene: 他不小心把膝盖擦伤了。 He accidentally scraped his knee.
sceneCN: 这里 scrape 是「擦伤」（第 2 个义项）；句意：他不小心把膝盖擦伤了。

senses.title: To rub against a surface
senses.definition: to rub something hard against a surface
senses.definitionCN: 使某物用力摩擦表面
senses.example: She scraped the paint off the door.
senses.exampleCN: 她把门上的漆刮掉了。
senses.why: The core sense is harsh rubbing that removes a layer.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是摩擦表面并带走一层。

senses.title: To wound the skin
senses.definition: to damage the skin by rubbing it against something rough
senses.definitionCN: 因摩擦粗糙表面而伤到皮肤
senses.example: He accidentally scraped his knee.
senses.exampleCN: 他不小心把膝盖擦伤了。
senses.why: The rubbing action becomes a small injury.
senses.whyCN: 摩擦动作变成一种小伤。

senses.title: To barely succeed
senses.definition: to succeed by a very small margin
senses.definitionCN: 以极小差距成功
senses.example: He scraped through the test.
senses.exampleCN: 他勉强通过了考试。
senses.why: Passing by a scrape is passing by a narrow margin.
senses.whyCN: 「擦着边通过」就是以极小差距通过。

senses.title: To gather with effort
senses.definition: to collect something with difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 困难地收集某物
senses.example: They scraped together enough money.
senses.exampleCN: 他们凑齐了足够的钱。
senses.why: Scraping the last bits together means gathering what is left.
senses.whyCN: 刮拢最后一点，就是收集剩余之物。

intro.en: Scrape probably comes from Old Norse skrapa, to scratch or scrape.
intro.cn: scrape 可能源自古诺尔斯语 skrapa（刮、擦）。

items.en: Skrapa meant to scratch or scrape a surface.
items.cn: skrapa 意为刮擦表面。

items.en: Scrapen meant to remove something by rubbing.
items.cn: scrapen 意为通过摩擦去除某物。

items.en: Scrape also meant to scratch the skin.
items.cn: scrape 也开始表示擦伤皮肤。

items.en: Scraping together meant collecting with difficulty.
items.cn: scrape together 意为艰难地凑集。

items.en: Scrape through means to pass by a narrow margin.
items.cn: scrape through 意为勉强通过。

note.en: Scrape is compared with similar-looking words and with verbs for rubbing and scratching.
note.cn: 把 scrape 与形近词以及表示摩擦和刮擦的动词作比较。

entries.definition: a small piece left over
to rub hard in order to clean
a steep slope
to mark a surface with a sharp point
to move with pressure over a surface
to break the skin by rubbing

normalIntro.en: Scrape is hard rubbing, and it also names a narrow escape.
normalIntro.cn: scrape 是用力摩擦，也指勉强过关。

normal.en: Scrape the pan to get the last bits.
normal.cn: 刮锅底以取得最后一点食物。

normal.en: Scrape a knee on rough ground.
normal.cn: 在粗糙地面擦伤膝盖。

normal.en: Scrape through means barely pass.
normal.cn: scrape through 意为勉强通过。

normal.en: Scrape together means collect with effort.
normal.cn: scrape together 意为费力凑集。

normal.en: A scraper is a tool for scraping.
normal.cn: scraper 是刮擦工具。

abstract.en: The word is about surfaces and what lies just beneath them.
abstract.cn: 这个词关涉表面以及表面之下的一层。

abstract.en: A narrow pass is like a near miss that still touches.
abstract.cn: 勉强通过就像擦着边的险胜。

abstract.en: Gathering by scraping is collecting what barely remains.
abstract.cn: 刮拢式收集就是收集几乎不剩的东西。

examples.en: She scraped the paint off the door.
examples.cn: 她把门上的漆刮掉了。

examples.en: He scraped through the test.
examples.cn: 他勉强通过了考试。

examples.en: They scraped together enough money.
examples.cn: 他们凑齐了足够的钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: scrape 可能与古诺尔斯语 skrapa（刮）有关，核心动作是「用硬物摩擦表面」；勉强通过考试就像「擦着边过去」。

root: 可能源自古诺尔斯语 skrapa（刮、擦），核心义「用硬物摩擦表面并带走一层」。

sensesIntro.en: Scrape means to rub a surface, wound the skin, barely succeed, or gather with effort.
sensesIntro.cn: scrape 意为刮擦表面、擦伤皮肤、勉强成功，或费力凑集。

core.en: Hard contact that removes or wounds.
core.cn: 带走表层或造成伤害的强力接触。

branches.en: Rubbing a layer off a surface.
branches.cn: 把表层从物体上摩擦掉。

branches.en: Damaging skin against something rough.
branches.cn: 被粗糙物擦伤皮肤。

branches.en: Passing with almost no margin.
branches.cn: 几乎没有余量地通过。

branches.en: Collecting what is left with difficulty.
branches.cn: 困难地收集剩余之物。

branches.en: The same action can remove paint or skin.
branches.cn: 同一个动作可以刮掉漆，也可以擦伤皮肤。

intro.en: Scrape forms tools, fragments, and phrasal verbs.
intro.cn: scrape 构成工具、碎屑与短语动词。

latinIntro.en: Old Norse skrapa is the likely source; there is no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: 古诺尔斯语 skrapa 是可能来源，没有拉丁词根。

items.meaning: to rub hard, or a scrape mark

items.example: They scraped the old paper away.

items.meaning: the act or sound of scraping

items.example: Use a scraper on the ice.
The scrapings went into the bin.
items.exampleCN: 刮下的碎屑被倒进垃圾桶。

items.meaning: to pass by a narrow margin

items.exampleCN: 我们勉强凑齐了一支队伍。

definition_zh: 妥协；折中；妥协方案；危及
definition_en: an agreement in which each side accepts less than it wanted
core_image: 两个人各退半步，在中间那条线上握手
scene: 谈价谈到天黑，买卖双方各让一步才成交。 After hours of argument, they reached a compromise.
sceneCN: 这里 compromise 指「妥协方案」（第 1 个义项：双方各让一步达成的安排）；句意是争论几个小时后，他们达成了一个折中方案。

senses.title: A deal with give and take
senses.definition: an arrangement in which both sides give up part of what they want
senses.definitionCN: 双方都放弃部分要求的安排
senses.example: Both sides accepted a compromise on price.
senses.exampleCN: 双方接受了价格上的折中方案。
senses.why: Two wishes cannot both be fully met, so each side bends a little.
senses.whyCN: 两个愿望无法都完全满足，于是各自弯一点。

senses.title: Settle by giving way
senses.definition: to end an argument by each side giving up something
senses.definitionCN: 通过各方放弃一些东西来结束争论
senses.example: They compromised and shared the cost.
senses.exampleCN: 他们各让一步，分摊了费用。
senses.why: The verb names the act that produces the noun.
senses.whyCN: 动词命名的是产生这个名词的动作。

senses.title: Put something at risk
senses.definition: to weaken or damage something such as safety or quality
senses.definitionCN: 削弱或损害安全、质量等东西
senses.example: Never compromise on safety.
senses.exampleCN: 在安全上绝不能让步。
senses.why: If you give away a principle, you also put what depends on it in danger.
senses.whyCN: 让掉一条原则，依赖它的东西也就陷入危险。

intro.en: Compromise comes from Latin compromittere, to promise together, and named an agreement to accept an arbiter's decision.
intro.cn: compromise 来自拉丁语 compromittere（共同承诺），最初指共同接受仲裁者裁断的约定。

items.en: Com- meant together and promittere meant to promise.
items.cn: com- 表示一起，promittere 表示承诺。

items.en: Compromittere meant to bind both sides by a promise.
items.cn: compromittere 意为用承诺约束双方。

items.en: Old French compromis named the agreement itself.
items.cn: 古法语 compromis 指这份约定本身。

items.en: English compromise first meant a joint promise to accept a ruling.
items.cn: 英语 compromise 最初指共同承诺接受裁断。

items.en: It widened to any deal in which both sides give way.
items.cn: 后来它扩展到任何双方让步的交易。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words close in shape to compromise, and the meaning group names other words for settling a dispute.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 compromise 形状相近的词，近义组列出其他表示了结争执的词。

entries.definition: to consist of particular parts
a statement that you will do something
a calm state of mind
an arrangement accepted by both sides
something given up to end an argument
an official end to a disagreement

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with two people stepping toward the middle, then move to risk and to shared cost.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从两个人向中间迈步开始，再走到风险与分摊费用。

normal.en: Com- is together and promise is a pledge, so a compromise is a pledge both sides keep.
normal.cn: com- 是一起，promise 是承诺，compromise 就是双方都守的承诺。

normal.en: Each side walks half the distance and meets in the middle.
normal.cn: 双方各走一半路，在中间相遇。

normal.en: A compromise is not a defeat; it is a shared saving of the deal.
normal.cn: 妥协不是失败，而是共同保住这笔交易。

normal.en: Compromise safety and the whole plan is at risk.
normal.cn: 危及安全，整个计划就都处在风险中。

normal.en: An uncompromising person refuses to move at all.
normal.cn: 一个 uncompromising 的人一步也不肯动。

abstract.en: Picture two hands meeting over the middle of a table.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手在桌子中央上方握到一起。

abstract.en: Picture a rope pulled from both ends until each side shortens.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳从两端被拉，直到两边都变短。

abstract.en: Picture a door neither side can close alone.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇任何一方都无法独自关上的门。

examples.en: The two leaders finally reached a compromise.
examples.cn: 两位领导人最终达成了妥协。

examples.en: She refused to compromise on the quality of the material.
examples.cn: 她拒绝在材料质量上让步。

examples.en: Cheap repairs may compromise the safety of the bridge.
examples.cn: 廉价维修可能危及这座桥的安全。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 compromise 记成 com（一起）加 promise（承诺）：双方一起许下各让一步的承诺，就是妥协。

root: 源自拉丁语 compromittere（com 一起 + promittere 承诺），本义是共同承诺接受裁断，后指双方各让一步达成的妥协，并引申为危及。

sensesIntro.en: From a joint promise to accept a ruling, to a deal with give and take, and finally to the risk of giving too much away.
sensesIntro.cn: 从共同承诺接受裁断，到各让一步的交易，最后到让得太多所带来的风险。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people each stepping half way and shaking hands on the middle line.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人各走半步，在中间那条线上握手。

branches.en: The noun names the agreement that ends the distance.
branches.cn: 名词指结束这段距离的那份约定。

branches.en: The verb names the act of stepping toward the middle.
branches.cn: 动词指向中间迈步的动作。

branches.en: Giving way on a principle creates a new kind of danger.
branches.cn: 在原则上让步，会产生一种新的危险。

branches.en: Deal and act are the same event seen as noun and verb.
branches.cn: 交易与动作是同一件事的名词与动词两面。

branches.en: Both involve giving something away, for peace or at a cost.
branches.cn: 两者都涉及让出东西，或为和平，或付出代价。

intro.en: Compromise is built on Latin com-, together, plus promittere, to promise, through the French form compromis.
intro.cn: compromise 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 promittere（承诺）构成，经法语 compromis 进入英语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin promise base also gives promise, promising and promissory.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的承诺词基还给出 promise、promising 与 promissory。

items.example: Small compromises kept the talks alive.
items.exampleCN: 一些小妥协让谈判得以继续。

items.example: The system was compromised by a virus.
items.exampleCN: 系统被病毒侵入而受损。

items.example: He was known as a practical compromiser.
items.exampleCN: 他以务实的妥协者著称。
这些信坦率得有损声誉。
她采取了不妥协的立场。

items.example: She kept her promise to return.

definition_en: without being affected by something; paying no attention to a difficulty or a warning
core_image: 雨幕中的跑道上，一个人仍按原来的节奏跑圈
scene: 雨越下越大，操场上的人却没有停，仍按原来的节奏跑圈。 The team kept training regardless of the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 regardless 是「不管」（第 1 个义项：不受某事影响）；句意为球队不顾下雨，照常训练。画面里可留意：越来越大的雨、没有停下的脚步。

senses.title: Without being affected
senses.definition: in spite of something, without letting it change what happens
senses.definitionCN: 尽管有某事，也不让它改变要做的事
senses.example: The team kept training regardless of the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 球队不顾下雨，照常训练。
senses.why: The suffix means without, and the stem means looking: the word describes a person who does not look at the obstacle.
senses.whyCN: 后缀意为「没有」，词干意为「看」：这个词描述一个不去看障碍的人。

senses.title: In any case
senses.definition: used alone to mean that something will happen whatever else is true
senses.definitionCN: 单独使用时，表示无论其他情况如何某事都会发生
senses.example: The bridge may be closed, but we are going regardless.
senses.exampleCN: 桥也许封了，但无论如何我们都要去。
senses.why: The same ignoring of conditions becomes an adverb of stubborn intent: the plan goes on, rain or no rain.
senses.whyCN: 同样是对条件的无视，转为副词便表示倔强的意图：计划照走，下不下雨都一样。

intro.en: Regardless is regard with a suffix meaning without: it names the attitude of one who does not look at what stands in the way.
intro.cn: regardless 是 regard 加上意为「没有」的后缀：它命名一种不去看阻碍的态度。

items.en: The French verb meant to look at closely, and English shortened it to regard.
items.cn: 这个法语动词意为仔细地看，英语把它简省为 regard。

items.en: Regard kept the sense of a look and of a care, both of which the suffix can cancel.
items.cn: regard 保留「看」与「关切」两义，而后缀能把两者都取消。

items.en: The English suffix -less comes from a Germanic word meaning free of or without.
items.cn: 英语后缀 -less 出自一个意为「没有、免于」的日耳曼词。

items.en: The adjective and adverb regardless appeared in the eighteenth century and spread quickly in speech.
items.cn: 形容词与副词 regardless 出现在十八世纪，并很快在口语中流行。

items.en: The phrase regardless of became the standard way to name a condition that is not allowed to matter.
items.cn: regardless of 这一短语成为表示「不把某条件当作回事」的标准说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of looking and not looking; the near-meaning group gathers expressions of ignoring conditions.
note.cn: 形近组收表示「看」与「不看」的词；近义组收表示无视条件的说法。

Mindful and attentive.

normalIntro.en: The word says look-less: no looking at the obstacle, so the plan continues as it was.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词说的是「不看」：不看障碍，所以计划照旧继续。

normal.en: Regard plus less: without looking at the thing in the way.
normal.cn: regard 加 less：不去看挡路的东西。

normal.en: Regardless of the weather means the rain will not stop us.
normal.cn: regardless of the weather 指下雨也拦不住我们。

normal.en: Going regardless is a stubborn kind of courage.
normal.cn: going regardless 是一种倔强的勇气。

normal.en: The suffix less cancels the looking in regard.
normal.cn: 后缀 less 取消了 regard 中的「看」。

normal.en: Do not confuse regardless with regardful, which means full of care.
normal.cn: 别把 regardless 与 regardful 弄混，后者意为充满关切。

abstract.en: To act regardless is to decide that a warning will not be a reason.
abstract.cn: 不顾一切地行动，就是认定某个警告不能成为理由。

abstract.en: Some obstacles deserve a look before they are ignored.
abstract.cn: 有些障碍在被无视之前，值得先看一眼。

abstract.en: Courage without regard is often only haste.
abstract.cn: 不顾一切的勇气，常常只是急躁。

examples.en: The team kept training regardless of the rain.
examples.cn: 球队不顾下雨，照常训练。

examples.en: The bridge may be closed, but we are going regardless.
examples.cn: 桥也许封了，但无论如何我们都要去。

examples.en: She applied for the job regardless of her lack of experience.
examples.cn: 尽管缺乏经验，她还是申请了这份工作。

root: 古法语 regarder（仔细看）→ 英语 regard（看待）＋ -less（没有）→ regardless；词根非拉丁语，因此不列拉丁条目。同族有 regard、disregard、regardful。

sensesIntro.en: The core is not looking at an obstacle; the senses move from an act done in spite of something to the adverb of going on anyway.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「不去看障碍」；义项从不顾某事而行动，到「无论如何也要去」的副词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a runner holding the same pace while the rain grows heavier.

branches.cn: 大雨中的训练

branches.en: the same pace kept to the end

intro.cn: 一个表「看」的词接上表「没有」的后缀，合成词便命名「选择不看挡路之物」的态度。

latinIntro.en: The stem regard is French of Germanic origin, and the suffix -less is English; no Latin root is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 词干 regard 是源自日耳曼语的法语词，后缀 -less 属英语，因此不列拉丁词根。

definition_en: enlarged because of injury, liquid, or pressure
core_image: 扭伤的脚踝鼓起来，皮肤绷得发亮
scene: 他扭伤后脚踝肿了。 His ankle was swollen after the fall.
sceneCN: 这里 swollen 是「肿胀的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：摔倒后他的脚踝肿了。

senses.title: Enlarged by injury or liquid
senses.definition: larger than normal because of fluid or injury
senses.definitionCN: 因液体或受伤而比正常更大
senses.example: His ankle was swollen after the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 摔倒后他的脚踝肿了。
senses.why: The past participle of swell keeps the picture of something filling and rising.
senses.whyCN: swell 的过去分词保留了某物被填满并隆起的画面。

senses.title: Increased in size or amount
senses.definition: made larger in size or number
senses.definitionCN: 在体积或数量上变大
senses.example: The swollen budget worried the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 膨胀的预算让委员会担忧。
senses.why: What fills with liquid can also fill with numbers, so size itself can be swollen.
senses.whyCN: 能充满液体的也能充满数字，因此规模本身也可以「膨胀」。

senses.title: Rising above its banks
senses.definition: having more water than usual, as a river
senses.definitionCN: 水位高于平常的，如河流
senses.example: The swollen river swept away the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 涨水的河流冲走了桥。
senses.why: A river that swells rises like injured flesh, so the same word describes both.
senses.whyCN: 上涨的河像肿起的皮肉一样隆起，于是同一个词兼指两者。

intro.en: Swollen is the past participle of swell, an old Germanic verb for growing larger.
intro.cn: swollen 是 swell 的过去分词，源自表示变大的古老日耳曼语动词。

items.en: The root meant to grow or become big.
items.cn: 该词根意为生长或变大。

items.en: Swellan meant to swell or grow.
items.cn: swellan 意为膨胀或生长。

items.en: Swollen became the past participle of swellen.
items.cn: swollen 成为 swellen 的过去分词。

items.en: Swollen described injured or inflamed flesh.
items.cn: swollen 描述受伤或发炎的皮肉。

items.en: Swollen extended to rivers, budgets and pride.
items.cn: swollen 扩展到河流、预算与骄傲。

note.en: Swollen is compared with look-alike words and with words for being enlarged.
note.cn: 把 swollen 与形近词以及表示变大的词作比较。

an enlarged area
to move down quickly
red and painful

normalIntro.en: Swollen describes anything filled until it rises above its usual shape.
normalIntro.cn: swollen 描述被填满而隆起、超出平常形状的任何东西。

abstract.en: A swollen river and a swollen ego both forget their banks.

abstract.en: To be swollen is to hold more than you can carry.

definition_zh: 中等的；适度的；温和的；使缓和；主持
definition_en: neither large nor small; not extreme in opinion; to make something less intense; and to preside over a discussion
core_image: 炉火被一只手掌轻轻压住，火苗不旺也不灭
scene: 会议的圆桌旁，两个人声音越来越高，主持人抬手示意双方停一停，把话头接了过去。 The chair tried to moderate a debate that had turned personal.
sceneCN: 这里是「主持、居中调解」（第 4 个义项：引导讨论并控制节奏）；句意为主席试图把一个已经变成人身攻击的辩论拉回正轨。图中可辨识物件：圆桌、麦克风、凉掉的茶水。

derivatives.zh: 由 moderate 加 -ly 构成，义为「适度地；有节制地」
由 moderate 加 -ion 构成，义为「适度；节制」
由 moderate 加 -or 构成，义为「主持人；调解人」
由否定前缀 im- 加 moderate 构成，义为「过度的；无节制的」

senses.title: Neither very large nor very small
senses.definition: of a size, amount or level that sits between the extremes
senses.definitionCN: 处在两端之间的大小、数量或水平
senses.example: Hire a car of moderate size for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 租一辆中等大小的车用一周。
senses.why: Latin modus meant a measure, and moderatus described what is kept inside its measure, so the adjective starts from a proper limit rather than from the middle point itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 modus 意为尺度，moderatus 描述的是被保持在尺度之内的东西，所以这个形容词的起点是「有恰当的界限」，而不是「正中间那一点」。

senses.title: Not extreme in opinion
senses.definition: holding views that avoid the extremes, especially in politics or religion
senses.definitionCN: 尤指在政治或宗教上不持极端立场
senses.example: Her moderate views made her acceptable to both camps.
senses.exampleCN: 她温和的立场让两个阵营都能接受她。
senses.why: A person who stays inside measure in argument was called moderate, because the same limit that governs quantity also governs how far an opinion should go.
senses.whyCN: 在争论中守住尺度的人被称为 moderate，因为约束数量的那条界限，也同样约束一种观点可以走多远。

senses.title: To make less intense
senses.definition: to make a feeling, force or rate become less strong or less fast
senses.definitionCN: 使情绪、力量或速度变得不那么强烈或快速
senses.example: The doctor moderated the dose after the fever dropped.
senses.exampleCN: 退烧之后医生把剂量调低了。
senses.why: The verb came from the same participle: to moderate is to put something back inside its measure, which in practice means turning down what has grown too strong.
senses.whyCN: 动词出自同一个分词：to moderate 就是把某样东西重新放回尺度之内，落到实际里就是把长过头的东西压下去。

senses.title: To preside over a discussion
senses.definition: to lead a debate or discussion and keep it orderly and fair
senses.definitionCN: 引导辩论或讨论，使其有序而公正
senses.example: She moderated the panel without letting anyone dominate.
senses.exampleCN: 她主持座谈，没让任何人独占话语。
senses.why: A chair does to a conversation what the adjective does to a quantity: keeps it within limits, so the verb moved from controlling force to controlling talk.
senses.whyCN: 主席对谈话做的事，正如形容词对数量做的事——把它守在界限内；于是动词从控制力量走到了控制发言。

intro.en: Moderate comes from Latin moderatus, the participle of moderari, to keep something within a measure, and that measure is modus.
intro.cn: moderate 出自拉丁语 moderatus，它是 moderari（把某物守在尺度内）的分词，而那条尺度就是 modus。

items.en: Modus meant a measure, a due amount or a manner, and it is the small noun inside a large family of English words about limits and ways.
items.cn: modus 意为尺度、适当的分量、方式，它是英语里一大族关于界限与方式的词所共有的那个小名词。

items.en: Moderari meant to keep within measure, to set a limit or to guide, and it was used of weather, of temper and of people in charge.
items.cn: moderari 意为守在尺度内、设定界限或引导，既用于天气与脾气，也用于掌事的人。

items.en: Its participle moderatus described what had been held inside its measure, and from that participle English took the adjective.
items.cn: 它的分词 moderatus 描述已经被守在尺度内的东西，英语的形容词正是从这个分词来的。

items.en: English borrowed moderate in the fifteenth century as an adjective of quantity and of temper, then formed the verb from it.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入 moderate，用作数量与脾气的形容词，随后又由它造出动词。

items.en: Modern English added the public sense of presiding over a debate, where the limit being kept is the order of the discussion rather than the strength of anything.
items.cn: 现代英语加上了主持辩论的公共义，此时被守住的界限是讨论的秩序，而不是某样东西的强度。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin measure word modus through its English family; the near-meaning group gathers words for what stays mild or within bounds.
note.cn: 形近组顺着拉丁语「尺度」modus 及其英语词族展开；近义组收表示温和或守在有界之内的词。

entries.definition: The quality of keeping things within sensible limits.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物守在有分寸的界限内的品质。

entries.definition: A person who chairs a discussion and keeps it orderly.
entries.definitionCN: 主持讨论并维持秩序的人。

entries.definition: Going far beyond a sensible limit.
To a limited but not small degree.
entries.definitionCN: 程度有限但不算小的；适度地。

entries.definition: Not strong or severe in effect.
Kept within limits, especially of climate or of appetite.
entries.definitionCN: 尤指气候或欲望被守在限度之内的。

entries.definition: Not large in size or amount; not boastful.
entries.definitionCN: 规模或数量不大的；不自夸的。

entries.definition: Held back from going too far.
entries.definitionCN: 被克制住、不走得太远的。

normalIntro.en: A Latin word for measure runs through this family, so every member is about staying inside a line rather than about being weak.
normalIntro.cn: 一个拉丁语的「尺度」贯穿这个词族，所以每个成员说的都是「守在一条线内」，而不是「软弱」。

normal.en: Modus, the Latin word for measure, sits inside moderate, moderation and immoderate, so all three talk about limits.
normal.cn: modus 是拉丁语「尺度」，它藏在 moderate、moderation 与 immoderate 里，所以这三个词说的都是界限。

normal.en: Moderari is the verb of keeping within measure, and the adjective moderatus plus English moderate are its direct descendants.
normal.cn: moderari 是「守在尺度内」的动词，形容词 moderatus 与英语 moderate 都是它的直系后代。

normal.en: Adding -ly gives moderately, -ion gives moderation, -or gives the person who keeps order, so one stem makes adverb, noun and person.
normal.cn: 加 -ly 得 moderately，加 -ion 得 moderation，加 -or 得那个维持秩序的人，一个词干造出副词、名词和人。

normal.en: Im- before moderate reverses it, so immoderate is exactly what has escaped its measure.
normal.cn: im- 加在 moderate 前面把意思反转，于是 immoderate 正是「跑出尺度之外」的东西。

normal.en: The debate sense shows the metaphor at work: a chair keeps the talk inside bounds, as a doctor keeps a dose inside bounds.
normal.cn: 辩论义把这个比喻摆了出来：主席把发言守在范围内，正如医生把剂量守在范围内。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressing down on a flame that has grown too high, lowering it without putting it out.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手按住蹿得过高的火苗，把它压低却不弄灭。

abstract.en: A single word covers a medium size, a calm opinion and a chaired debate, because all three are about staying inside a line.
abstract.cn: 同一个词涵盖了中等尺寸、平和的立场和被主持的辩论，因为三者都在讲「守在一条线内」。

abstract.en: Moderation is not the absence of force but its measured release, which is why the same verb can calm a fever and steer a panel.
abstract.cn: 节制不是没有力量，而是有分寸地释放力量，所以同一个动词既能退烧，也能引导一场座谈。

examples.en: Hire a car of moderate size for a week.
examples.cn: 租一辆中等大小的车用一周。

examples.en: The doctor moderated the dose after the fever dropped.
examples.cn: 退烧之后医生把剂量调低了。

examples.en: She moderated the panel without letting anyone dominate.
examples.cn: 她主持座谈，没让任何人独占话语。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「莫得瑞特」——做事莫要特别过头，守住中间那一段；记住 moderate 是适度的，也是使缓和、主持讨论。

root: 拉丁语 modus（尺度、方式）派生动词 moderari（守在尺度内），其过去分词 moderatus 构成形容词 moderate；同族词有 moderation、moderator、immoderate。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a kept measure; the senses divide into medium size, calm opinion, a force turned down, and a discussion kept in order.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「守住的尺度」；义项由此分出中等的尺寸、平和的立场、被调低的力量，以及被维持秩序的讨论。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressing a flame down to a steady, moderate height.

definition_zh: 第一百万个；百万分之一；第百万次
definition_en: the ordinal form of one million, naming the item at position one million; also one of a million equal parts, and in speech a wearisome millionth repetition
core_image: 博物馆门口的花束藏在门后的桌下，计数器停在最后一格，只等下一只手推开门
scene: 博物馆入口的计数器停在九十九万九千九百九十九，工作人员把一束花藏进门后的桌下，等着下一位推门进来的人。 The staff shook hands with the millionth visitor and handed her the flowers.
sceneCN: 这里是「第一百万个」（第 1 个义项：序数意义的第一百万位）；句意为工作人员与第一百万位参观者握手，并把花递给她。图中可辨识物件：计数器、藏在桌下的花束、入口大门。

pos.zh: 第一百万个；百万分之一
第一百万的；百万分之一的

derivatives.zh: 去掉序数词尾 -th 得到的基数词，义为「百万」
million 加 -fold（倍）构成，义为「百万倍地」
million 加 -aire（表人后缀）构成，义为「百万富翁」

senses.title: The item at position one million
senses.definition: the person or thing that comes at position one million in a long series, counted from the first
senses.definitionCN: 在一个很长的序列里，从第一个数起排在第一百万位的那个人或物
senses.example: The millionth copy rolled off the press just before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 第一百万份在黎明前下了印刷机。
senses.why: English builds ordinals with -th, the same ending that makes fourth and tenth, so millionth simply marks the place that follows the nine hundred ninety-nine thousand nine hundred ninety-ninth item.
senses.whyCN: 英语用 -th 构成序数，和 fourth、tenth 用的是同一个词尾，所以 millionth 只是标出紧跟在九十九万九千九百九十九之后的那一位。

senses.title: One of a million equal parts
senses.definition: a fraction equal to one divided by a million, one piece of a whole cut into a million equal pieces
senses.definitionCN: 等于一除以一百万的分数，即把整体切成一百万等份后的一份
senses.example: The laser flashes once every millionth of a second.
senses.exampleCN: 激光每百万分之一秒闪一次。
senses.why: Latin had millesimus for a thousandth part, and English applies the same fraction logic one step higher: cut a whole into a million equal pieces, and any single piece is a millionth.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语本有 millesimus 表示千分之一，英语把同样的分数逻辑再往上推一级：把整体切成一百万等份，随便一份都是百万分之一。

senses.title: The millionth repetition, said in weariness
senses.definition: the millionth time something happens, used in speech to mean far too many repetitions rather than an exact count
senses.definitionCN: 某事发生的第百万次，口语里用来指重复得没完没了，而不是精确计数
senses.example: For the millionth time, would you please close the door?
senses.exampleCN: 跟你说了多少回了，能不能把门关上？
senses.why: A million repetitions are past anyone's patience, so the phrase for the millionth time drifted from exact counting into a complaint about endless repetition.
senses.whyCN: 重复一百万次早已超过任何人的耐心，于是「第百万次」这个说法从精确计数滑成一句抱怨，指没完没了的重复。

intro.en: The ordinal is younger than the number it orders: Latin already had a word for a thousandth, but English millionth was built on the English noun with the ordinary ordinal ending.
intro.cn: 序数形式比它所排序的数更年轻：拉丁语早就有「千分之一」的词，而英语的 millionth 是拿英语名词加寻常的序数词尾造出来的。

items.en: Latin had mille for a thousand and millesimus for the thousandth, so the ordinal pattern behind millionth is older than the word itself.
items.cn: 拉丁语有 mille（千）和 millesimus（第一千），所以 millionth 背后的序数模式比这个词本身更老。

items.en: The base noun million was coined in Italian from mille plus the augmentative -one, naming a big thousand.
items.cn: 基数词 million 在意大利语里由 mille 加增大后缀 -one 造出，意为「大一号的千」。

items.en: French adopted million and used it in accounts and chronicles before English took it over.
items.cn: 法语收下 million，先在账目与编年史里使用，之后才被英语接过去。

items.en: English million named the exact number first, and the ordinal followed once people needed to point at a particular item in a series that long.
items.cn: 英语的 million 先指精确的数；等人们需要指出这么长的序列里的某一项时，序数形式才跟上。

items.en: Millionth was formed in English by adding -th to million on the model of fourth and tenth, and later spread into phrases of tired repetition.
items.cn: millionth 是在英语里照 fourth、tenth 的样子给 million 加 -th 造出的，后来又扩展到表示疲惫重复的说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the forms built on the same million and the same ordinal ending; the near-meaning group gathers the fractions and position words that sit around it on the scale.
note.cn: 形近组收由同一个 million 与同一个序数词尾构成的词；近义组收在同一把尺子上围绕它的分数词与位置词。

entries.definition: One of a billion equal parts, a far smaller slice than a millionth.

entries.definition: A part of a whole, especially one produced by dividing it into equal pieces.
entries.definitionCN: 整体的一部分，尤指等分之后得到的一份。

entries.definition: A number word that marks position in a series rather than quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 标出序列中的位置而不是数量的数词。

normalIntro.en: A Latin thousandth gave the model, the Italian big thousand gave the base, and English supplied the ordinary ordinal ending that turned it into a position and a fraction.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「千分之一」提供了样板，意大利语的「大一号的千」提供了基数，英语再添上寻常的序数词尾，把它变成位置与分数。

normal.en: Latin already had millesimus for the thousandth, so the shape of millionth was waiting long before million existed.
normal.cn: 拉丁语早有 millesimus 表示第一千，millionth 的骨架在 million 出现之前就已备好。

normal.en: Million was coined in Italian from mille and the suffix -one, which makes a word mean a larger version of its base.
normal.cn: million 是意大利语用 mille 加后缀 -one 造出的，那个后缀让词表示「基词的大一号」。

normal.en: English adds -th to million exactly as it adds it to four and ten, so the ordinal is ordinary building, not a new root.
normal.cn: 英语给 million 加 -th，和给 four、ten 加 -th 一模一样，是寻常构词，不是新词根。

normal.en: The plural millionths turns the ordinal into a countable fraction, one of a million equal slices.
normal.cn: 复数 millionths 把序数变成可数的分数，即一百万等份中的一份。

normal.en: For the millionth time is a phrase of impatience, because nobody can count that far and the number has become a way of saying again and again.
normal.cn: for the millionth time 是一句不耐烦的话，因为没人真能数到那里，这个数成了「一遍又一遍」的说法。

abstract.en: A museum counts every visitor, and the number that ends the counting is the one that gets the flowers.
abstract.cn: 博物馆数着每一位来客，而给数划上句号的那一位才会拿到花。

abstract.en: The same word can mean a prize position, a sliver of time, and a complaint about repetition, because all three are ways of being at the far end of a count.
abstract.cn: 同一个词可以指一个获奖的位置、一小片时间、一句关于重复的抱怨，因为三者都是「数到尽头」的方式。

abstract.en: Being first is ordinary; being the millionth is only a story because somebody chose to keep counting.
abstract.cn: 成为第一个很平常；成为第一百万个之所以成故事，只因有人愿意一直数下去。

intro.en: Continent comes from Latin continens, continuous or holding together, from continere, to hold together, built from com-, together, and tenere, to hold.
intro.cn: continent 来自拉丁语 continens（连绵不断、连在一起），源于 continere（保持在一起），由 com-（一起）与 tenere（握住）构成。

items.en: Tenere meant to hold or keep in the hand.
items.cn: tenere 意为握住或保持在手中。

items.en: Continere meant to hold things together as one.
items.cn: continere 意为把事物保持为一个整体。

items.en: Continens described land that runs on without a break.
items.cn: continens 形容连绵不断、没有中断的陆地。

items.en: The noun terra continens, the continuous land, was shortened in use.
items.cn: 短语 terra continens（连成一片的陆地）在使用中被省略。

items.en: English continent named the great landmasses of the globe.

items.en: It also means the mainland seen from an island.
