dict_mnemonic.text: 把 continent 记成 con（一起）加 tin（握住）：一大片土地被海围住、始终连在一起，就是大陆。

root: 源自拉丁语 continens（连绵不断的），来自 continere（保持在一起），由 con-（一起）与 tenere（握住）构成。

sensesIntro.en: From one great land held together by the sea, to the mainland that an island looks toward.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被海围住的巨大陆块，到岛屿所遥望的大陆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brown landmass ringed by one thin line of surf.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块褐色陆地，被一线白浪围住。

branches.en: The largest division of land gets its own name.
branches.cn: 最大的一级陆地区域有了自己的名字。

branches.en: An island measures itself against the mainland.
branches.cn: 岛屿以大陆为参照来衡量自己。

branches.en: Both senses rest on land that holds together.
branches.cn: 两个义项都立足于连成一片的陆地。

branches.en: A continent is defined by the water around it.
branches.cn: 大洲由它周围的水来界定。

branches.en: The mainland is a continent seen from a smaller shore.
branches.cn: 大陆是从较小海岸望去的大洲。

intro.en: Continent is built on Latin com-, together, plus tenere, to hold.
intro.cn: continent 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 tenere（握住）构成。

latinIntro.en: The holding base ten- also appears in contain, retain and tenant.
latinIntro.cn: 握持词基 ten- 也出现在 contain、retain 与 tenant 中。

items.meaning: land held together as one mass
items.example: They crossed the continent by rail.

items.exampleCN: 洲际航班要飞好几个小时。

items.meaning: a large land area slightly smaller than a continent
items.meaningCN: 比大洲略小的大片陆地
items.example: The river feeds a whole subcontinent.
items.exampleCN: 这条河养活了整个次大陆。

items.meaning: to keep holding on without a break
to keep something rather than lose it
a person who holds a rented place

definition_zh: 指挥；导体；售票员；列车员
definition_en: a person who directs an orchestra, or a material that carries heat or electricity
core_image: 音乐厅里，指挥棒尖带着整支乐队起落
scene: 列车员沿着车厢一路检票。 The conductor checked every ticket on the train.
sceneCN: 这里 conductor 指「列车员」（第 3 个义项：在车上查票的工作人员）；句意是列车员在火车上逐一查票。

pos.zh: 指挥；导体；售票员；列车员

senses.title: Leader of an orchestra
senses.definition: a person who stands in front of musicians and directs their playing
senses.definitionCN: 站在乐手前方、指挥他们演奏的人
senses.example: The conductor raised her baton and the hall fell silent.
senses.exampleCN: 指挥举起指挥棒，音乐厅立刻安静下来。
senses.why: Many players need one pair of hands to set the same beat.
senses.whyCN: 许多乐手需要一双手来定下同一个节拍。

senses.title: A material that carries energy
senses.definition: a substance that allows heat or electricity to pass through it
senses.definitionCN: 允许热或电通过的物质
senses.example: Copper is a common conductor of electricity.
senses.exampleCN: 铜是常见的电导体。
senses.why: Some materials let energy walk through them instead of blocking it.
senses.whyCN: 有些材料让能量从内部通过，而不是把它挡住。

senses.title: Ticket officer on a vehicle
senses.definition: a person on a bus or train who checks or sells tickets
senses.definitionCN: 在公交或列车上查票、卖票的工作人员
senses.example: The conductor asked to see our tickets.
senses.exampleCN: 列车员要求查看我们的车票。
senses.why: The same word for leading now names the one who keeps a journey in order.
senses.whyCN: 同一个表示带领的词，如今指维持旅程秩序的人。

intro.en: Conductor comes from Latin conductor, one who leads together, from conducere, to lead together.
intro.cn: conductor 来自拉丁语 conductor，意为把大家带领在一起的人，源自 conducere（一起带领）。

items.en: Conducere meant to bring people or things under one lead.
items.cn: conducere 意为把人与物收拢到同一个带领之下。

items.en: Conductor named a person who hired or guided others.
items.cn: conductor 指雇用或带领他人的人。

items.en: English conductor first meant a guide or a leader.
items.cn: 英语 conductor 最初指引导者或领导者。

items.en: It came to name the person who directs an orchestra.
items.cn: 后来它开始指指挥管弦乐队的人。

items.en: It also names materials that carry heat or electricity and staff who check tickets.
items.cn: 它也指传导热或电的材料，以及在车上查票的工作人员。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words built on the same Latin lead base, and the meaning group names other people who guide or carry.
note.cn: 形近组收的是建立在同一拉丁词基上的词，近义组列出其他引导或运送的人。

entries.definition: the passing of heat through a material
a channel that carries water or wires
a company or person hired to do building work
a person who controls a group or an activity
a person who guides a group
a thing or person that carries something

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a baton in a concert hall, then move to copper wire and to a ticket punch.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从音乐厅里的指挥棒开始，再走到铜线与检票钳。

normal.en: Conduct plus -or is the person who conducts.
normal.cn: conduct 加 -or，就是做这件事的人。

normal.en: The conductor does not play a note, yet the whole hall follows her hands.
normal.cn: 指挥一个音都不演奏，整个音乐厅却都跟着她的手。

normal.en: A conductor lets electricity pass, just as a guide lets people pass.
normal.cn: 导体让电流通过，正如向导让人群通过。

normal.en: On an old bus, the conductor walks down the aisle with a ticket machine.
normal.cn: 在老式公交车上，售票员拿着售票机走过过道。

normal.en: One root, four jobs: leading, carrying, selling and checking.
normal.cn: 同一个词根，四种工作：带领、传导、售票与查票。

abstract.en: Picture a thin white stick cutting the air in four beats.
abstract.cn: 想象一根白色细棒在空中划出四拍。

abstract.en: Picture a copper thread glowing under a lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象一根铜线在灯下微微发亮。

abstract.en: Picture a small metal punch biting a paper ticket.
abstract.cn: 想象一把小金属钳在纸票上咬出一个洞。

examples.en: The conductor smiled and the orchestra began.
examples.cn: 指挥微微一笑，乐团开始演奏。

examples.en: Rubber is a poor conductor of electricity.
examples.cn: 橡胶是电的不良导体。

examples.en: The conductor helped an old man find his seat.
examples.cn: 列车员帮一位老人找到了座位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 conductor 记成 conduct（带领、传导）加 or（人）：带领乐团的人是指挥，让电通过的东西是导体，在车上管秩序的人是列车员。

root: 源自拉丁语 conductor（con 一起 + ducere 引导 + or 人），本义是带领者，后指乐队指挥、导体与车上售票查票的人。

sensesIntro.en: From one who leads a group, to a material that carries energy, and finally to the officer who keeps a journey in order.
sensesIntro.cn: 从带领团体的人，到输送能量的材料，最后到维持旅程秩序的车上职员。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand with a baton, a copper wire, and a ticket punch all doing one job of carrying.
core.cn: 核心意象：握指挥棒的手、一根铜线、一把检票钳，都在做同一件传送的事。

branches.en: The musical sense is the clearest picture of leading together.
branches.cn: 音乐义项是「一起带领」最清楚的画面。

branches.en: A conductor of electricity carries energy without using it up.
branches.cn: 电导体输送能量，自身并不消耗它。

branches.en: The ticket officer leads a journey by keeping it in order.
branches.cn: 查票的职员靠维持秩序来带领一段旅程。

branches.en: Both stand in front of a group and keep it moving.
branches.cn: 两者都站在一群人前面，让这群人继续前进。

branches.en: Baton and wire both pass something along a clear line.
branches.cn: 指挥棒与电线都沿一条清晰的线传递某种东西。

intro.en: Conductor is Latin com-, together, plus ducere, to lead, with the person ending -or.
intro.cn: conductor 由拉丁语 com-（一起）、ducere（引导）与表示人的词尾 -or 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin lead base duct- also appears in conduct and product.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的引导词基 duct- 也出现在 conduct 与 product 中。

items.meaning: more than one leader or carrier
items.exampleCN: 两位指挥共同负责这场音乐会。

items.example: The conductor chose a slow tempo.
items.exampleCN: 指挥选了一个较慢的速度。

items.example: He will conduct the final concert.
items.exampleCN: 他将指挥最后一场音乐会。

items.meaning: the movement of heat through matter

items.example: The gel is conductive and safe.
items.exampleCN: 这种凝胶导电而且安全。

items.meaning: how well a material carries energy
items.example: They measured the conductivity of the sample.
items.exampleCN: 他们测量了样品的传导性。

items.meaning: a material between a conductor and an insulator
items.example: The chip is made of a semiconductor.
items.exampleCN: 这块芯片由半导体制成。

definition_zh: 修改；调整；修饰；缓和；修订；改性
definition_en: to change something in some details or qualities without replacing it entirely, often to make it fit a new purpose or to make it less extreme
core_image: 在一件旧物上按尺寸修整几处，整体仍然是原来那件东西
scene: 工程师没有换掉整只阀门，只改了一个法兰让它接上新管道。 The engineer did not replace the whole valve; she chose to modify one flange so that it would fit the new pipe.
sceneCN: 这里 modify 是「部分修改」（第 1 个义项：改动局部而不整体替换）；句意：工程师没有换掉整个阀门，只改动了一个法兰盘，让它能接上新管道。场景要点：一台拆开的旧阀门、一只被换掉的零件、旁边保留完好的阀体；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 修改；调整；修饰；缓和；修订

senses.title: Change a part, not the whole
senses.definition: to change some details, parts, or qualities of something while leaving its identity and main structure intact
senses.definitionCN: 改动某物的部分细节、部件或性质，同时保留它的身份与主要结构
senses.example: The engineer modified the valve instead of replacing the whole assembly.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师改动了阀门，而不是更换整个组件。
senses.why: Latin modificare joined modus 'measure' to facere 'make': to make according to a measure. The word starts from adjusting a thing's proportions, not from destroying and remaking it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 modificare 把 modus“尺度”与 facere“做”合在一起：按尺度去制作。这个词的起点是调整一件东西的比例，而不是毁掉重造。

senses.title: Adapt to fit a new use
senses.definition: to adjust something so that it suits a different purpose, condition, or user
senses.definitionCN: 调整某物，使其适合不同的目的、条件或使用者
senses.example: The school modified its timetable to fit the bus schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 学校调整了课程表，以配合公交时刻。
senses.why: A measure is taken against a purpose. When the purpose changes, the thing is re-measured and trimmed until it fits again, which is why modify often appears with 'to fit' or 'for'.
senses.whyCN: 尺度总是对着某个目的量。目的变了，东西就被重新量一遍、修一遍，直到重新合身，所以 modify 常与“适应”“为了”一类说法连用。

senses.title: Grammar: a word limits another
senses.titleCN: 语法：一个词限定另一个词
senses.definition: of a word or phrase, to limit or qualify the meaning of another word
senses.definitionCN: 指一个词或短语限定或说明另一个词的意义
senses.example: In 'a red door', the adjective modifies the noun 'door'.
senses.exampleCN: 在 a red door 中，形容词修饰名词 door。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the word for narrowing a meaning. An adjective places a measure on a noun, saying which part of its range is meant, without replacing the noun.
senses.whyCN: 语法学借这个词来表示收窄意义。形容词给名词加上一个尺度，说明指的是它范围里的哪一部分，而不替换这个名词。

senses.title: Soften a claim or tone
senses.definition: to make a statement, demand, or tone less absolute or less severe
senses.definitionCN: 使陈述、要求或语气不那么绝对、不那么严厉
senses.example: He modified his tone when he saw that the child was listening.
senses.exampleCN: 看到孩子在听，他把语气缓和了下来。
senses.why: To keep within measure also means not to exceed it. A demand that is modified has been brought back inside reasonable bounds, so the word can mean 'soften' rather than 'change'.
senses.whyCN: 保持在尺度之内，也意味着不越过尺度。被 modify 的要求被拉回到合理的范围内，所以这个词可以表示“缓和”，而不只是“改变”。

senses.title: Amend a legal text
senses.definition: to make a formal, limited change to a law, contract, or official document
senses.definitionCN: 对法律、合同或正式文件作有限度的正式改动
senses.example: The council modified the payment clause but left the rest of the contract untouched.
senses.exampleCN: 理事会修改了付款条款，但合同其余部分未动。
senses.why: A legal document is changed clause by clause, never rewritten wholesale if it can be helped. Modify is the natural verb for a bounded edit that leaves the instrument in force.
senses.whyCN: 法律文件是一条款一条款地改，不到万不得已不会整份重写。modify 正是表示这种有限改动、让文件继续有效的动词。

senses.title: Change a setting or file
senses.definition: in computing, to change the contents, settings, or code of a file or system
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机领域，改动文件或系统的内容、设置或代码
senses.example: Do not modify the system files without a backup.
senses.exampleCN: 没有备份时不要修改系统文件。
senses.why: Software is a structure with many settable measures. Editing one setting or one line modifies the system: the rest keeps running, which is exactly the partial-change picture.
senses.whyCN: 软件是一个有许多可调尺度的结构。改一项设置或一行代码就是 modify 系统：其余部分照旧运行，这正是“局部改动”的画面。

senses.title: Rewrite a gene
senses.definition: in biology, to change an organism's genetic material, often to give it a new trait
senses.definitionCN: 在生物学中，改变生物体的遗传物质，常为赋予它新的性状
senses.example: The scientists modified one gene in the rice plant to resist drought.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家改动了水稻的一个基因，使其抗旱。
senses.why: The organism is not replaced; one instruction inside it is re-measured and rewritten. The phrase 'genetically modified' keeps the sense of a targeted edit to an existing living thing.
senses.whyCN: 生物体本身没有被替换，被改写的是它内部的一条指令。“genetically modified”这一说法保留了“对既有生物做定点改动”的意思。

senses.title: Alter a material's surface
senses.definition: in materials science, to change the properties of a surface or structure without changing its bulk
senses.definitionCN: 在材料科学中，改变表面或结构的性能，而不改变其主体
senses.example: The coating modifies the surface without changing the bulk of the metal.
senses.exampleCN: 这层涂层改变了金属的表面性能，却没有改变其主体。
senses.why: Here the measure is applied only to the skin of the object. The bulk stays as it was, which makes modify the right verb for a treatment rather than a replacement.
senses.whyCN: 这里的尺度只施加在物体的表皮上。主体保持原样，因此 modify 适合表示一种处理，而不是替换。

senses.title: A sound changed by its neighbour
senses.titleCN: 语音受邻音影响而变化
senses.definition: in phonetics, of a sound, to be changed under the influence of a neighbouring sound
senses.definitionCN: 在语音学中，指一个音受相邻音影响而发生改变
senses.example: In rapid speech, the final sound is often modified by the sound that follows it.
senses.exampleCN: 在快速语流中，末尾的音常被后面的音改变。
senses.why: A sound keeps its identity but shifts its shape to fit its neighbours, just as a part is trimmed to fit a new pipe. The word's 'fit' sense is at work even here.
senses.whyCN: 一个音保留自己的身份，却改变形状去适应相邻的音，正如一个零件被修整以接上新管道。即便在这里，这个词“适配”的意思仍在起作用。

intro.en: Modify entered English from Old French in the late fourteenth century and goes back to Latin modificare, literally 'to make by measure'. Its two Latin parts, modus and facere, explain why it means partial adjustment rather than total replacement. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: modify 在 14 世纪晚期从古法语进入英语，可追溯到拉丁语 modificare，字面意为“按尺度制作”。它的两个拉丁成分 modus 与 facere，解释了它为何表示局部调整而不是整体替换。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded as modifien, 'alter, amend, adjust, change the properties, form, or function of'. It also meant 'set limits, keep within the bounds of reason; choose a middle course'.
items.cn: 最早记录为 modifien，意为“改变、修正、调整、改变……的性质、形式或功能”。它还有“设定界限、保持在理性范围之内、选择中间道路”的意思。

items.en: The English verb came through Old French modifier (14c.), which already carried the sense of altering something to fit.
items.cn: 这个英语动词经古法语 modifier（14 世纪）而来，后者已经带有“改动某物使其适配”的意思。

items.en: Latin modificare meant 'to limit, measure off, restrain'. It joined modus 'measure, manner' with the combining form of facere 'to make'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 modificare 意为“限定、量出、约束”。它把 modus“尺度、方式”与 facere“制作”的结合形式合在一起。

items.en: Modus goes back to PIE *med- 'take appropriate measures', the root behind mode, moderate, and modest. Facere goes back to PIE *dhe- 'to set, put', the root behind do and deed.
items.cn: modus 可追溯到原始印欧语 *med-“采取恰当的尺度”，也是 mode、moderate、modest 的词根。facere 可追溯到原始印欧语 *dhe-“放置、安放”，也是 do 与 deed 的词根。

items.en: Modification is recorded c. 1500 in philosophy, 'determination by a mode or quality'. Modifier appears in the 1580s as 'one who or that which modifies'; its grammatical sense is from 1865. The 'result of a variation' sense of modification is from the 1660s, and 'act of altering' from 1774.
items.cn: modification 约 1500 年出现在哲学中，意为“由某种模式或性质所决定”。modifier 于 16 世纪 80 年代出现，指“修改者或修改之物”；其语法义始于 1865 年。modification 的“变化结果”义始于 17 世纪 60 年代，“改变的行为”义始于 1774 年。

items.en: Moderate comes from Latin moderari 'keep within measure', the same *med- root but a different branch. Adjust comes from Old French ajouster, from Late Latin adjuxtare 'bring near'. Alter comes from Latin alter 'the other of two'. Each changes something in a different direction or degree.
items.cn: moderate 来自拉丁语 moderari“保持在尺度之内”，同出 *med- 词根，但属于另一分支。adjust 来自古法语 ajouster，源于晚期拉丁语 adjuxtare“使靠近”。alter 来自拉丁语 alter“两者中的另一个”。它们各自以不同方向或不同程度改变事物。

note.en: The first group separates the noun, the agent, and the two participles built on modify; the second compares verbs of change that learners too often use as exact synonyms.
note.cn: 第一组把由 modify 构成的名词、施动者与两个分词分开；第二组比较学习者常当作完全同义词的几个“改变”动词。

entries.definition: a change made to something, or the act of changing it. It names the change or the process, while modify names the doing.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物所作的改动，或改动这一行为。它命名改动或过程，而 modify 命名动作本身。

entries.definition: one who or that which modifies; in grammar, a word that limits another word. It is the doer or the tool, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 修改者或修改之物；语法中指限定另一词的词。它是施动者或工具，不是动作。

entries.definition: changed in some parts, as in 'genetically modified' or 'a modified version'. It describes the result, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 局部被改动的，如“转基因的”或“修改过的版本”。它描述结果，而不是过程。

entries.definition: not changed at all. The un- prefix marks the absence of exactly the partial edit that modify performs.
entries.definitionCN: 完全未被改动的。un- 前缀标记的正是 modify 所做的那种局部改动的缺席。

entries.definition: to change something slightly so that it fits, works, or looks right. It stresses fitting a standard or a position, while modify can also mean changing a design or a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 轻微改变某物，使其合适、正常或位置正确。它强调对准某个标准或位置，而 modify 还可指改动设计或规则。

entries.definition: to make something different, often in a way that changes its character or appearance. It is broader and can suggest a deeper change than modify.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物不同，常指改变其性质或外观。它范围更广，也可能暗示比 modify 更深的改变。

entries.definition: to change a text, law, or agreement in order to correct or improve it. It is mostly formal and textual, whereas modify also covers objects and behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 为纠正或改进而改动文本、法律或协议。它多用于正式文本，而 modify 也覆盖物件与行为。

entries.definition: to make something less extreme or less intense, or to preside over a discussion. It shares the 'measure' root but works mainly on strength, not on form.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物不那么极端或强烈，或主持讨论。它与 modify 共享“尺度”词根，但主要作用于强度，而不是形式。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin modus 'measure' plus facere 'make', and the English family modification, modifier, mode, and moderate.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 modus“尺度”加 facere“制作”，以及英语词族 modification、modifier、mode、moderate。

normal.en: modus is 'measure' and -ify comes from facere 'make'. To modify is to make according to a measure, which is why the thing keeps its identity.
normal.cn: modus 是“尺度”，-ify 来自 facere“制作”。modify 就是按尺度去制作，所以被改的东西保留自己的身份。

normal.en: The Latin verb also meant 'set limits, keep within bounds', so modifying a demand can mean softening it rather than changing its content.
normal.cn: 这个拉丁动词还意为“设定界限、保持在范围之内”，所以修改一项要求可以是把它放缓，而不是改变内容。

normal.en: modification is the change or the act; modifier is the person or word that does it; modified is the result.
normal.cn: modification 是改动或改动行为；modifier 是做这件事的人或词；modified 是结果。

normal.en: mode, moderate, modest and modify all share *med- 'take appropriate measures', but only modify adds the 'make' part.
normal.cn: mode、moderate、modest、modify 都共享 *med-“采取恰当尺度”，但只有 modify 加了“制作”这一部分。

normal.en: In grammar the word narrows meaning: an adjective modifies a noun without replacing it, the same partial-change picture.
normal.cn: 在语法里这个词收窄意义：形容词修饰名词而不替换它，仍是那幅“局部改动”的画面。

abstract.en: Picture a craftsman with a ruler beside an old chair. He shaves one leg, keeps the frame, and the chair is still the same chair.
abstract.cn: 想象一位工匠把尺子放在一把旧椅子旁。他刨短一条腿，保留框架，椅子仍是同一把椅子。

abstract.en: Modify is a dial, not a switch: it turns the value a little, while replace would swap the whole unit out.
abstract.cn: modify 是一个旋钮，不是开关：它把数值稍微转动一点，而 replace 会把整个部件换掉。

abstract.en: Every modified thing still answers to its old name; if it no longer does, it was not modified but replaced.
abstract.cn: 每一件被 modify 的东西仍回应它原来的名字；如果它不再回应，那它不是被修改，而是被替换了。

examples.en: We modified the proposal after the first round of comments.
examples.cn: 第一轮意见之后，我们修改了提案。

examples.en: The app lets you modify the layout without changing the underlying data.
examples.cn: 这个应用允许你修改布局，而不改动底层数据。

examples.en: Some crops were modified to grow in salt water, but the yield remains low.
examples.cn: 有些作物被改造为能在咸水中生长，但产量仍然很低。

dict_mnemonic.text: “摸得改”——先摸清原有尺寸，再动手改那几处，整体不换 → modify 修改、调整（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 modificare“按尺度制作”，由 modus“尺度”加 facere“制作”构成，核心是“按尺寸修整局部，而不整体替换”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of modify, all from one gesture: a measure is laid on an existing thing and a few parts are trimmed, while the thing itself remains what it was.
sensesIntro.cn: modify 的九个义项都来自同一个动作：把尺子放在既有之物上，修整其中几处，而物件本身仍是原来的物件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a few parts trimmed to measure, the whole left standing.
core.cn: 核心意象：按尺寸修整几处，整体仍然立着。

branches.en: PARTIAL CHANGE: details or parts are re-measured, either to improve the thing or to fit a new use.
branches.cn: 局部改变：细节或部件被重新量过，或为改良物件，或为适配新用途。

branches.en: GRAMMAR: a word places a measure on another word and narrows its meaning without replacing it.
branches.cn: 语法：一个词给另一个词加上尺度，收窄它的意义，而不替换它。

branches.en: BOUNDS AND TEXT: a tone or demand is brought back inside measure, and a legal clause is edited while the document stays in force.
branches.cn: 尺度与文本：语气或要求被拉回尺度之内，法律条款被改动而文件继续有效。

branches.en: SYSTEMS AND GENES: one setting, one line of code, or one gene is changed while the rest keeps running.
branches.cn: 系统与基因：一项设置、一行代码或一个基因被改动，其余部分照旧运行。

branches.en: SURFACE AND SOUND: only the skin of a material, or the shape of a sound, is adjusted to fit its surroundings.
branches.cn: 表面与语音：只调整材料的表皮或一个音的形状，使其适应周围环境。

intro.en: Modify is a Latin verb whose English shape joins mod- 'measure' to -ify 'make'. The same stem, with -ation, -er, -ed, -able and un-, produces the rest of the family.
intro.cn: modify 是拉丁语动词，其英语形态把 mod-“尺度”与 -ify“制作”合在一起。同一词干加上 -ation、-er、-ed、-able 与 un-，构成其余词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin modificare combined modus 'measure' and facere 'make'. Facere also gives -fic-, -fect, and -fy in English, which is why modify, manufacture, and effect all contain a 'making' piece.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 modificare 把 modus“尺度”与 facere“制作”合起来。facere 在英语里还给出 -fic-、-fect 与 -fy，所以 modify、manufacture、effect 都含有一个“制作”的成分。

items.meaning: to make according to measure; to change in part
items.meaningCN: 按尺度制作；局部改变（mod- 尺度 + -ify 使……）
items.example: They modified the engine to burn less fuel.
items.exampleCN: 他们改动了发动机，使其更省油。

items.meaning: a change, or the act of changing
items.meaningCN: 修改；改动（-ation 构成行为名词）
items.example: The design needs only a small modification.
items.exampleCN: 这个设计只需要做一处小改动。

items.meaning: one who modifies; a grammatical qualifier
items.meaningCN: 修改者；修饰语（-er 表施动者）
items.example: In the phrase 'very cold', 'very' is a modifier.
items.exampleCN: 在 very cold 这一短语中，very 是修饰语。

items.meaningCN: 被局部改动的（-ed 构成过去分词）
items.exampleCN: 修改后的版本运行得更快。

items.meaningCN: 未修改的（un- 否定 + modified）
items.example: The control group used unmodified seed.
items.exampleCN: 对照组使用的是未经改造的种子。

items.example: The settings are modifiable by the user.
items.exampleCN: 这些设置可由用户修改。

items.meaning: a user-made change to a game
items.meaningCN: 模组；游戏修改版（modification 的截短）
items.example: He installed a mod that adds new maps.
items.exampleCN: 他安装了一个增加新地图的模组。

items.example: The device has a low-power mode.
items.exampleCN: 这个设备有一个低功耗模式。

items.meaning: kept within measure; to reduce intensity
items.meaningCN: 适度的；使缓和（保持在尺度内）
items.example: She moderated her criticism in public.
items.exampleCN: 她在公开场合缓和了自己的批评。

items.meaning: a person's usual way of working
items.meaningCN: 一贯做法；做事方式（拉丁语“工作的方式”）
items.example: The thief's modus operandi was always the same.
items.exampleCN: 这个窃贼的作案手法始终如一。

items.meaning: to treat something as a commodity
items.meaningCN: 使商品化（com- 共同 + mod- 尺度 + -ify 使……）
items.example: Critics say the festival has commodified local music.
items.exampleCN: 批评者说这个节日把本地音乐商品化了。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 限定；量出；约束（modus 尺度 + facere 制作）

definition_zh: 乐观的；乐观主义的；抱乐观看法的
definition_en: expecting good things to happen or believing that a situation will turn out well, especially when the signs are not encouraging
core_image: 半杯水前，一个人盯着杯里剩下的那一半，嘴角微微上扬
scene: 桌上只剩半杯水，屋里的人却说明天还会有人送水来，语气平稳。 She stayed optimistic even after the second rejection letter arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 optimistic 是「乐观的」（第 1 个义项：对结果抱有好转的期待）；句意为第二封拒信到了，她仍然保持乐观，画面是桌上半杯水与平稳的语气。

pos.zh: 乐观的；乐观主义的；抱乐观看法的

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 optimum（最好的事物）经法语 optimisme 进入英语，义为「乐观主义」
由 optimism 加表示「持某种看法的人」的后缀 -ist 构成，义为「乐观的人」
由 optimistic 加副词后缀 -ally 构成，义为「乐观地」
由 over- 与 optimistic 复合而成，义为「过于乐观的」

senses.title: Expecting a good outcome
senses.definition: believing that something good will happen or that a situation will end well
senses.definitionCN: 相信会有好事发生，或相信局面最终会好转
senses.example: She is optimistic about her chances of getting the job.
senses.exampleCN: 她对自己拿到那份工作抱乐观态度。
senses.why: Latin optimum named the best possible thing, so the word begins with the best outcome already in view.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 optimum 指「可能最好的事物」，所以这个词一开始就把最好的结果放在眼前；期望自然朝好的方向走，这是最直接的一层。

senses.title: Remaining hopeful despite unfavourable signs
senses.titleCN: 即使迹象不利仍怀希望的
senses.definition: keeping a hopeful view even when the evidence so far is discouraging
senses.definitionCN: 即便目前的迹象令人泄气，仍保持有希望的看法
senses.example: He remained optimistic after the first two plans failed.
senses.exampleCN: 头两个方案失败后，他仍然保持乐观。
senses.why: If the best outcome is what the mind fixes on, a setback is read as temporary rather than final.
senses.whyCN: 既然心里认定的是最好的结果，挫折就会被读成暂时的，而不是定局；这个义项强调在不利证据面前仍不改判断。

senses.title: Characteristic of the belief that good prevails
senses.definition: belonging to the outlook that treats the world or human affairs as tending towards good
senses.definitionCN: 属于认为世界或人事总体趋向好的那种看法
senses.example: The report takes an optimistic view of the region's economy.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告对该地区经济持乐观看法。
senses.why: The word also labels a whole outlook, not just a mood, because optimism grew into a name for a way of judging the world.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也能标一整套看法，而不只是一时情绪，因为 optimism 已经成了判断世界的一种立场之名；形容词便跟着承担这层立场色彩。

intro.en: Optimistic is a nineteenth-century adjective built on optimism, a word formed from Latin optimum, the best possible thing.
intro.cn: optimistic 是十九世纪在 optimism 上造出的形容词，而 optimism 由拉丁语 optimum（可能最好的事物）构成。

items.en: Optimus was the irregular superlative of bonus, good, so it meant the best of all.
items.cn: optimus 是 bonus（好的）的不规则最高级，意为「最好的」。

items.en: Optimum named the greatest good or the best possible state, and it gave the later word its target.
items.cn: optimum 指最大的善或可能达到的最佳状态，为后来的词提供了目标。

items.en: French optimisme was coined in the eighteenth century for the view that this world is the best that could exist.
items.cn: 法语 optimisme 于十八世纪造出，用来指「这个世界已是可能存在的最好世界」的看法。

items.en: English borrowed optimism, added optimist for a person who holds it, and formed optimistic with -ic.
items.cn: 英语借入 optimism，加 -ist 指持此看法的人，再用 -ic 造出 optimistic。

items.en: Modern English uses optimistic for a hopeful expectation in daily life, not only for the philosophical doctrine.
items.cn: 现代英语把 optimistic 用在日常生活里「抱有希望」的期待，不再只指哲学学说。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Latin best-word and its English family; the near-meaning group gathers words for hope, confidence and a bright temper.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「最好」这个词及其英语同族；近义组收表示希望、信心与明朗性情的词。

entries.definition: The belief that good things are likely or that the world tends towards good.
entries.definitionCN: 相信好结果可能出现、或世界趋向好的看法。

entries.definition: A person who expects good things to happen.
The best or most favourable point or condition.
entries.definitionCN: 最好或最有利的点与状态。

entries.definition: Best possible for a given purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 在特定目的下最好的；最优的。

entries.definition: Feeling that something desired may still happen.
entries.definitionCN: 觉得想要的事仍可能发生。

entries.definition: Thinking in a confident and constructive way.
entries.definitionCN: 以自信、建设性的方式思考。

entries.definition: Sure that something will succeed or be right.
entries.definitionCN: 确信某事会成功或正确。

entries.definition: In good spirits and inclined to see the bright side.
entries.definitionCN: 心情好，倾向于看好的一面。

normalIntro.en: The word carries the Latin word for the best, so its hooks return to the best outcome, the person who expects it and the outlook that names it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词带着拉丁语「最好」的含义，记忆钩子都回到最好的结果、期待它的人，以及以此为名的看法。

normal.en: Optimum means the best possible thing, so optimistic starts by fixing the eyes on the best outcome.
normal.cn: optimum 意为可能最好的事物，所以 optimistic 一开始就把目光钉在最好的结果上。

normal.en: -ist names the person and -ic names the quality, so optimist and optimistic are two faces of one belief.
normal.cn: -ist 指人，-ic 指性质，所以 optimist 与 optimistic 是同一种信念的两张面孔。

normal.en: The opposite is pessimistic, built on pessimus, the worst, and the pair measures one scale from both ends.
normal.cn: 反义词 pessimistic 建在 pessimus（最坏的）上，两个词从两端量同一把尺。

normal.en: Optimistic about is the usual frame, and the preposition points the hope at a particular object.
normal.cn: optimistic about 是常见框架，介词把希望指向某个具体对象。

normal.en: Cautiously optimistic shows the word can be softened, because hope may be held with reservations.
normal.cn: cautiously optimistic 说明这个词可以加软化语，因为希望也可以带着保留。

abstract.en: A glass half full is the oldest picture of this word: the eye chooses which half to count.
abstract.cn: 半杯水是这个词最老的画面：眼睛选择去数哪一半。

abstract.en: A rejection letter that is folded but still answered is optimism turned into an action rather than a mood.
abstract.cn: 一封被折起却仍被回复的拒信，是乐观从情绪变成行动的样子。

abstract.en: A forecast of clearing skies after a grey week shows the word reaching forward to a future it cannot yet see.
abstract.cn: 灰暗一周之后「天气转晴」的预报，显示这个词在伸向它尚未看见的未来。

examples.en: She stayed optimistic even after the second rejection letter arrived.
examples.cn: 第二封拒信到了，她仍然保持乐观。

examples.en: The coach sounded optimistic about the team's chances.
examples.cn: 教练对球队的机会听起来很乐观。

examples.en: He is cautiously optimistic that the repairs will finish this week.
examples.cn: 他谨慎乐观地认为维修本周能完成。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「噢，盼它美」——optimistic 读来像盼着事情变美；盼好结果，就是乐观。

root: 拉丁语 optimus（最好的，bonus 的最高级）→ optimum（最佳）→ 法语 optimisme → 英语 optimism、optimist，再加 -ic 构成 optimistic。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the best outcome in view; the senses spread from expecting it, to holding on to it under bad signs, to a whole outlook that assumes good prevails.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「眼里最好的结果」；义项从期待它，扩展到在不利迹象下仍守住它，再扩展成假定善会占上风的整套看法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person before a half-filled glass, eyes fixed on the part that is still there.
core.cn: 核心意象：半杯水前的人，目光落在仍然存在的那一半。

branches.en: a half-filled glass and a steady gaze
branches.cn: 半杯水与平稳的目光

branches.en: a rejection letter folded but still answered
branches.cn: 被折起却仍被回复的拒信

branches.en: a report predicting a region's recovery
branches.cn: 预测某地区复苏的报告

branches.en: one hopeful reading, once of a glass and once of bad news
branches.cn: 同一种向好解读，一次落在水杯上，一次落在坏消息上

branches.en: a standing view of how the world tends to go
branches.cn: 对世界走向的固定看法

intro.en: The word rests on the Latin adjective for good and its superlative for best, then on the French and English nouns that turned that best into a doctrine.
intro.cn: 这个词依托拉丁语中表示「好」的形容词及其「最好」的最高级，再依托法语与英语名词，把「最好」变成一种主张。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: the view that the world is the best possible
items.meaningCN: 认为世界已达最佳的看法

items.meaning: a hopeful view of the future
a person who expects the best

definition_zh: 说出；发出（声音）；完全的；彻底的
definition_en: to say something or make a sound, or used of a complete state with nothing else mixed in
core_image: 一个人低声吐出两个字，声音轻得几乎听不见
scene: 黑暗里两个人靠墙坐着，其中一人终于开口，只吐出一句简短的道歉。 She was too tired to utter a single word.
sceneCN: 这里 utter 是「说出、发出」（第 1 个义项：用声音把话说出来）；句意为她累得一个字也说不出来。黑暗里轻轻吐出几个字的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 加名词后缀 -ance，义为「话语；言论」
加 -ly 构成副词，义为「完全地」
同源词，义为「最远的；极度的」

senses.title: To say something aloud
senses.definition: to say a word or a sentence, especially something short or final
senses.definitionCN: 说出一个词或一句话，尤指短促或决定性的话
senses.example: He did not utter a single word during the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 整个审判过程中他一个字也没说。
senses.why: The oldest form of the word meant putting out, and the voice puts breath and words out of the mouth.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的意思是「向外送出」，而声音正是把气息与话语从口中送出。

senses.title: To make a sound
senses.definition: to make a sound with the voice or with something else
senses.definitionCN: 用嗓音或别的东西发出声响
senses.example: The bird uttered a low whistle from the hedge.
senses.exampleCN: 那只鸟从树篱里发出一声低低的哨音。
senses.why: Once uttering means sending out breath, any sound can be sent out the same way.
senses.whyCN: 既然「说出」是把气息送出去，那么任何声音都可以照样送出去。

senses.title: Complete, with nothing else
senses.definition: used as an adjective of a state that is total, often with bad nouns
senses.definitionCN: 作形容词时形容某种状态是十足的，常与负面名词连用
senses.example: There was utter silence when the result was read out.
senses.exampleCN: 结果被念出时，一片寂静。
senses.why: The adjectival use follows the sense of going all the way out, so it means complete to the outermost degree.
senses.whyCN: 形容词用法承自「一直送到最外」的意思，所以它表示完整到了极点。

senses.title: The most complete kind of something
senses.definition: strengthening a noun such as failure or nonsense
senses.definitionCN: 用来加强失败、胡言这类名词的语气
senses.example: Calling the whole plan nonsense was an utter waste of a meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 把整个计划说成胡言，是白白浪费了一场会。
senses.why: Utter is almost never used for good nouns, so the adjective doubles as a signal of strong disapproval.
senses.whyCN: 这个词几乎不用在褒义名词上，因此这名形容词也成了强烈不赞同的信号。

intro.en: Two old senses, to send out and outermost, grew from the same Germanic root and have kept the same spelling.
intro.cn: 「向外送出」与「最外」两个古老意思都出自同一个日耳曼词根，并且拼写一直相同。

items.en: Uttrian meant to put out or drive out, from the adverb ut, out.
items.cn: uttrian 意为「放出、赶出」，来自副词 ut（向外）。

items.en: Utter and uttera meant outer, from the comparative of ut.
items.cn: utter 与 uttera 意为「外面的」，来自 ut 的比较级。

items.en: The verb extends from driving things out to giving voice to words.
items.cn: 这个动词从「把东西赶出去」扩展到「把话说出来」。

items.en: The adjective settles into the sense of complete, mostly before nouns of failure or silence.
items.cn: 形容词固定为「完全的」之义，多用在失败、寂静一类名词之前。

items.en: Utterance and utterly are the two surviving derivations in everyday use.
items.cn: utterance 与 utterly 是日常里留下的两个派生词。

note.en: The look-alike group shows the old out stem, and the near-meaning group divides speaking from complete states.
note.cn: 形近组展示古老的 out 词干，近义组按「说出」与「完全」两类意义分开。

normalIntro.en: One short word hides two lives: saying something aloud, and being complete to the last degree.
normalIntro.cn: 一个短词藏着两种生命：把话说出声来，以及完整到极点。

normal.en: Not utter a word is the fixed negative idiom.
normal.cn: not utter a word 是固定的否定说法。

normal.en: As an adjective it prefers bad nouns: utter nonsense and utter failure.
normal.cn: 作形容词时偏爱负面名词：utter nonsense、utter failure。

normal.en: Utterance is the noun, utterly the adverb.
normal.cn: 名词是 utterance，副词是 utterly。

normal.en: The adjective has no comparative form in normal use.
normal.cn: 这个形容词在正常用法中没有比较级。

normal.en: The same stem gives out and utmost, all pointing outward.
normal.cn: 同一词干给出 out 与 utmost，都指向「向外」。

abstract.en: Picture a whisper pressed out through the lips in a dark room.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗房间里一句话被嘴唇轻轻挤出。

abstract.en: Hear total silence after a verdict is read.
abstract.cn: 听判决念完之后那种彻底的安静。

abstract.en: See a plan collapse from the very first step.
abstract.cn: 看一个计划从第一步就彻底垮掉。

examples.en: He was so shocked that he could not utter a word.
examples.cn: 他震惊得一个字也说不出来。

examples.en: The meeting ended in utter silence.
examples.cn: 会议在一片彻底的沉默中结束。

examples.en: Everyone agreed the rumour was utter nonsense.
examples.cn: 大家都认同那传闻纯属胡言。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿特」——阿特一开口，说出的话就是十足的直白。

root: 古英语 ut（向外）：动词 uttrian（放出、说出）与形容词 uttera（外面的、彻底的）同出一源

sensesIntro.en: Sending breath outward gives the verb of speaking and of any sound, while the outward edge gives the adjective of complete states.
sensesIntro.cn: 把气息向外送出给出「说」与「发声」的动词义，而「最外之端」给出「彻底的」这一形容词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: words pushed out through the lips in the dark.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑暗里几个字被嘴唇挤出来。

branches.en: The speech branch: one word put out into the air.
branches.cn: 言语分支：一个字被送到空气里。

branches.en: The sound branch: voice or whistle sent out.
branches.cn: 声音分支：嗓音或哨音被送出。

branches.en: The adjective branch: a state complete to the edge.
branches.cn: 形容词分支：完整到边界的某种状态。

branches.en: The judgement branch: complete, and therefore strongly negative.
branches.cn: 评判分支：彻底，因而强烈否定。

branches.en: The breath branch: both speech and sound ride on outgoing breath.
branches.cn: 气息分支：说话与发声都靠呼出的气息。

intro.en: A Germanic root meaning outward, with no Latin inside; the two senses split early.
intro.cn: 一个意为「向外」的日耳曼词根，内部没有拉丁成分；两个义项很早就分开了。

latinIntro.en: The word has no Latin ancestor; the nearest Latin idea is the adverb extra, outside, which is listed for comparison only.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语祖源；最接近的拉丁概念是副词 extra（在外面），此处仅供对照。

items.example: The old root ut- means out.
items.exampleCN: 古老词根 ut- 意为向外。

items.example: Utter comes from driving something out.
items.exampleCN: utter 源自把东西送出去。

items.example: The verb ending marks the everyday action.
items.exampleCN: 动词词尾标记日常的反复动作。

items.example: Utterly means to the full degree.
items.exampleCN: utterly 意为达到完全的程度。

items.example: Out is the plain modern form.
items.exampleCN: out 是这个词的现代朴素形式。
inmost 是它内在的对称词。
